```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  exceptionHandler: const AppExceptionHandler(),
  // ...
);
```

## What render can return

`render` returns anything a controller can return: a `DoxResponse`, a map, a string.
Return the error itself (this is what `super.render` does) to get the default answer.

`req` is the raw `HttpRequest`. It is there even when the error came before Dox read the body.
Use it to read headers, like `req.headers.value('accept')`.

If `render` itself throws, Dox logs that error and sends the default answer.
The client always gets a response.

## Errors outside a request

Some errors do not belong to a request.
For example a future that nobody awaits, or an error in a service `shutdown()`.
Dox passes them to `report` too. The server keeps running.

## The response handler

The `responseHandler` of `AppConfig` still runs after `render`.
It sees every response, also error responses.
Use `render` to change errors, and `responseHandler` to change all responses (for example, to add a header).

See [Custom errors](../guides/custom-errors.md) for a full example with your own exception classes.


---

# Controller

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/controller/

# Controller

A controller holds the code that answers a route. It can be a class method, a static method or a plain function.

## Class based controller

Make one with the CLI:

```bash
dox create:controller Blog
```

It writes `lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart`.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  String index(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'all blogs';
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get<BlogController>('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.index);
```

`@Inject()` puts the controller in the container. Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add one.
The constructor can ask for services and repositories. See [Dependency injection](dependency-injection.md).

### Static method

```dart
class AppController {
  static String ping(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

Route.get('/ping', AppController.ping);
```

## Function based controller

```dart
String listBlog(DoxRequest req) {
  return 'all blogs';
}

Route.get('/blogs', listBlog);
```

## Resource controller

A resource controller has the 7 methods that `Route.resource` uses.

Make one with the CLI:

```bash
dox create:controller Blog -r
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  /// GET /resource
  Future<dynamic> index(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/create
  Future<dynamic> create(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// POST /resource
  Future<dynamic> store(DoxRequest req) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> show(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// GET /resource/{id}/edit
  Future<dynamic> edit(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// PUT|PATCH /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> update(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}

  /// DELETE /resource/{id}
  Future<dynamic> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {}
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.resource('blogs', BlogController);
```

You can delete methods you do not need. `Route.resource` skips them.
See [Routing: resource routes](routing.md#resource-routes).

## Parameters

A controller asks for what it needs by **type**. Dox fills each parameter.

```dart
Route.put<UserController>('/teams/{teamId}/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.update);

class UserController {
  Future<User> update(int teamId, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
}
```

| Parameter type | Dox gives |
| --- | --- |
| `DoxRequest` | the request |
| a `@Dto` class | the checked body or query. See [Validation](validation.md). |
| `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` | the path params, in the order of the route |
| the same types with `?` | an optional path param (`{id?}`). `null` when it is not in the URL. |
| a `@DoxModel` class | the model, loaded by the route param. See [route model binding](dependency-injection.md#route-model-binding). |
| an `@Inject()` class | the instance from the [container](dependency-injection.md#handler-parameters) |

Rules:

- The order of parameters is free. Path params are matched by position: the first path-param parameter gets the first `{...}` in the route.
- `DoxRequest` is not needed. Add it only when you use it.
- At most one `@Dto` parameter.
- Only positional parameters. Named and `[optional]` parameters are not supported.
- A catch-all `{path*}` param is a `String`.
- The same rules work for static methods and plain functions.
- Dox reads the parameter types once, at start. It does not use `dart:mirrors`.

**Path param types.** Dox converts the text from the URL:

- `int`: `"42"` is `42`. `"abc"` or `"4.5"` answers `404 Not Found`.
- `double`, `num`: `"4.5"` is `4.5`.
- `bool`: `true` or `1` is `true`. `false` or `0` is `false`.
- Any other text answers `404` too.
- Path params are checked first. When one is wrong, the DTO is not checked.

**Checked at start.** The server does not start when:

- a parameter type is not in the list above (did you run `dart run build_runner build`?),
- the method has more path-param parameters than the route has `{...}` params.

## What to return

Return a `String`, a `Map`, a model, a `File` and more. See [Response](response.md).


---

# Dependency injection

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/dependency-injection/

# Dependency injection

Dox has a container. It makes your classes and gives each constructor what it needs.
You do not register classes by hand.
Put `@Inject()` above a class, and `dox_builder` adds it to the container.
Dox does not use `dart:mirrors`. All the wiring is generated code.

## A full example

A repository reads the database. A service holds the business logic. A controller answers the route.

```dart title="lib/app/repositories/user.repository.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class UserRepository {
  Future<User?> find(int id) => User().find(id);
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/services/user.service.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/repositories/user.repository.dart';

@Inject()
class UserService {
  UserService(this.users);

  final UserRepository users;

  Future<User> show(int id) async {
    User? user = await users.find(id);
    if (user == null) throw NotFoundHttpException();
    return user;
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/services/user.service.dart';

@Inject()
class UserController {
  UserController(this.service);

  final UserService service;

  Future<User> show(int id) => service.show(id);
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get<UserController>('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show);
  }
}
```

Run the builder:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
```

It writes `lib/container.g.dart`. Give it to the app once:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
  // ...
);
```

That is all. `GET /api/users/5` makes the repository, the service and the controller, and calls `show(5)`.

## The generated file

`lib/container.g.dart` has one function. Each class gets a factory that calls its constructor.

```dart title="lib/container.g.dart"
// GENERATED CODE - DO NOT MODIFY BY HAND
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart' as i1;
import 'package:my_app/app/repositories/user.repository.dart' as i2;
import 'package:my_app/app/services/user.service.dart' as i3;
import 'package:my_app/routes/api.dart' as i4;
import 'package:my_app/services/orm_service.dart' as i5;
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart' as i6;

void registerContainer(IocContainer c) {
  c.singleton<i1.UserController>(
    (IocContainer c) => i1.UserController(c.get<i3.UserService>()),
  );
  c.singleton<i2.UserRepository>((IocContainer c) => i2.UserRepository());
  c.singleton<i3.UserService>(
    (IocContainer c) => i3.UserService(c.get<i2.UserRepository>()),
  );
  c.router<i4.ApiRouter>((IocContainer c) => i4.ApiRouter());
  c.service<i5.ORMService>((IocContainer c) => i5.ORMService());
  c.bindModel<i6.User>((String id) {
    int? key = int.tryParse(id);
    if (key == null) return null;
    return i6.User().find(key);
  });
}
```

Do not edit it. Run the builder again after you add a class.

## Lifetime

- `@Inject()`: one instance per isolate. It is made on first use.
- `@Inject(singleton: false)`: a new instance each time it is asked for.

Dox runs one server per isolate. Isolates do not share objects.
So each isolate runs `registerContainer` and has its own instances.
Do not keep state in a singleton that all isolates must see. Use the cache or the database for that.

## Constructor parameters

Each constructor parameter is found by its type.

- Positional and named parameters both work.
- An optional parameter whose type is not in the container keeps its default value.
- A nullable parameter whose type is not in the container gets `null`.
- Any other parameter whose type is not in the container stops the build.

## Routes to controller methods

Give the controller type, then a function that picks the method:

```dart
Route.get<PostController>('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
Route.post<PostController>('/posts', (PostController c) => c.store);
Route.put<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.update);
Route.delete<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.destroy);
```

The controller comes from the container. Dox gets it once per isolate, at start. A request does no extra work.
`.name()`, groups and middleware lists work the same:

```dart
Route.get<PostController>('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.show).name('posts.show');
Route.get<AuthController>('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (AuthController c) => c.me]);
```

You can leave out `<PostController>`. Dox then finds the controller by the parameter type: `Route.get('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index)`.

For resource routes, pass the class:

```dart
Route.resource('posts', PostController);
```

The method still gets its parameters as usual: `DoxRequest`, a `@Dto`, path params and bound models.
See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters).

## Handler parameters

A controller method (or a plain route function) can ask for any class of the container:

```dart
Route.get('/stats', (StatsService stats) => stats.today());
```

A singleton is read once, at start. A `singleton: false` class is made on each request.

## Route model binding

Every `@DoxModel` class gets a binder in `lib/container.g.dart`.
When a handler has a parameter of a model type, Dox loads the model by its primary key.

```dart
Route.get<PostController>('/posts/{post}', (PostController c) => c.show);

@Inject()
class PostController {
  Post show(Post post) => post;
}
```

- The route param with the name of the model is used: `{post}` for `Post`, `{blogPost}` for `BlogPost`.
- When there is no such param, the next route param in order is used, like `{id}`.
- A missing row answers `404`.
- An `int` key that is not a number answers `404`, with no database call.
- A route without a parameter of the model type does not load the model.
- A binder from `Route.bind` wins over this one. See [Routing: route model binding](routing.md#route-model-binding).

## Routers and services

You do not need `@Inject()` on them.

- Every class that extends `Router` is found. Its routes are registered at start.
- Every class that implements `DoxService` is found. Its `setup()` runs at start, in every isolate.

Their constructors get parameters from the container too.

They run in the order of their file path, then the order in the file.
To pick the order, list them in `AppConfig`:

```dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  container: registerContainer,
  services: <DoxService>[ORMService()], // runs first
  routers: <Router>[ApiRouter()],       // registered first
);
```

A listed class comes first. The others follow. No class runs twice.
A listed service is also the instance that the container gives.

## Use the container in code

`Dox().ioc` is the container of the current isolate.

```dart
UserService users = Dox().ioc.get<UserService>();
```

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get<T>()` | the instance of `T`. Throws when `T` is not registered. |
| `has<T>()` | `true` when `T` is registered |
| `singleton<T>(factory)` | one instance per isolate, made on first use |
| `factory<T>(factory)` | a new instance on each `get` |
| `instance<T>(value)` | `value` is the instance, eg. a config object |
| `override<T>(value)` | replace `T`, eg. with a fake in a test |
| `clearOverrides()` | remove every override |

## Tests

Replace a class with a fake before the app starts:

```dart
setUpAll(() async {
  Dox().ioc.override<UserRepository>(FakeUserRepository());
  client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
});

tearDownAll(() async {
  await client.close();
  Dox().ioc.clearOverrides();
});
```

An override stays when the app registers its classes again.
Call it before `DoxTestClient.start`. Controllers get their objects once, at start.

## Build errors

The build stops with a clear message when:

- a required parameter has a type that is not in the container,
- classes need each other in a circle. The message shows the chain, like `A -> B -> C -> A`,
- `@Inject()` is on an abstract class or a generic class,
- a class has no unnamed constructor.

## Limits

- Dox finds classes in `lib/` only.
- The container is keyed by the class. It does not map an interface to a class.
- Two classes with the same name in two files both work. But use the typed route style (`Route.get<C>(...)`) for them. They can not be handler parameters, because Dox can not tell them apart by name.


---

# Middleware

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/middleware/

# Middleware

Middleware is code that runs before the controller. Use it for checks like login, logging or rate limits.

## How it works

A middleware gets the request. It then does one of these:

- **Return the request.** Dox goes on to the next middleware, then to the controller.
- **Return something else** (a `String`, a `Map`, a `response(...)`). Dox sends it as the response. The controller does not run.
- **Throw an exception**, like `NotFoundHttpException()`. Dox sends the error response. See [Response: errors](response.md#errors).

A middleware can be `async`. Dox waits for it.

## Class based middleware

Create one with the CLI. It writes `lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart`.

```bash
dox create:middleware Logger
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // go on to the next middleware
  }
}
```

Then put it on a route:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get<WebController>('/ping', <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware(), (WebController c) => c.pong]);
```

!!! note
    `handle` takes an `IDoxRequest`, not a `DoxRequest`.

## Function based middleware

A function that takes a `DoxRequest` also works as middleware.

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/api_key.middleware.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

dynamic apiKeyMiddleware(DoxRequest req) {
  if (req.header('X-Api-Key') != 'secret') {
    return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Unauthorized'}).statusCode(401);
  }
  return req;
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.get<WebController>('/ping', <dynamic>[apiKeyMiddleware, (WebController c) => c.pong]);
```

## Many middleware on one route

Put them in the list before the controller. They run from left to right.
You can mix class and function middleware.

```dart
Route.get<WebController>('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  apiKeyMiddleware,
  (WebController c) => c.pong, // the controller is always last
]);
```

## Middleware for a group of routes

```dart
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', controller.me);
  Route.post('/logout', controller.logout);
});
```

## Middleware for a router or for all routes

For one router, set its `middleware` list:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()];

  @override
  void register() {
    // every route here runs LoggerMiddleware
  }
}
```

For all routes, set `globalMiddleware` in the app config:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  // ...
);
```

The order is: global middleware, then router middleware, then group middleware, then route middleware.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["Request"] --> G["Global<br>globalMiddleware"]
    G --> R["Router<br>middleware getter"]
    R --> P["Group<br>Route.middleware"]
    P --> T["Route<br>list before the controller"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S["Response"]
    G & R & P & T -.->|"returns a value or throws"| S
```

!!! tip "Built-in middleware"
    - `LogMiddleware` from `dox_core` writes one JSON log line per request. Body fields and headers whose name has `password`, `secret`, `token`, `authorization`, `cookie` or `api_key` in it (upper or lower case) are logged as `[REDACTED]`. Change the list with `redact:`. The new project turns it off when `APP_ENV` is `production`.
    - `AuthMiddleware` from `dox_auth` checks the JWT token. See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).
    - `RateLimit` from `dox_core` answers `429` when a client sends too many requests. See [Rate limiting](../security/rate-limiting.md).
    - `SecurityHeaders` from `dox_core` adds safe headers like `X-Frame-Options` to every answer. See [Security headers](../security/security-headers.md).


---

# Validation

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/validation/

# Validation

This page shows how to check request input with typed DTO classes.

Write a class with `@Dto()`. Ask for it in your controller.
Dox reads the request, checks it, and gives you a typed object.
When the input is wrong, Dox answers `422` with the errors. Your controller does not run.

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable, so optional

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email, this.age});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart"
class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email;
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}
```

## Setup

You do this once per app.

1. Make a DTO with `dox create:dto CreateUser`. It writes `lib/app/http/dtos/create_user.dto.dart`.
2. Run the generator: `dox build_runner:build` (or `dox build_runner:watch`).
   It writes a `.dto.g.dart` file next to each DTO, and one list of all DTOs in `lib/dtos.g.dart`.
3. Give that list to the app:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'package:my_app/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/dtos.g.dart
  // ...
);
```

Dox uses no reflection, so it needs this list to find your DTOs. Without it, the server stops at start with a clear error.

## Use a DTO

Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs.

```dart
Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async { ... }

// with the request and a path param
Future<User> update(DoxRequest req, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }
```

Or check inside the method. `req.validate<T>()` returns the object, or throws the `422` error.

```dart
CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();
```

See [Controller: parameters](controller.md#parameters) for the full rules.

## Required and optional

The Dart type decides. You do not write `required` or `nullable`.

| Field | Key missing | Value `null` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `final String name;` | error `required` | error `required` |
| `final int? age;` | `null` | `null` |
| `final Role role;` with `this.role = Role.user` | `Role.user` | error `required` |

- Rules on an optional field run only when it has a value.
- A default value is used only when the key is missing. The rules do not check it.
- **An empty string counts as missing.** So a required `String` rejects `""`. Add `@AllowEmpty()` to keep `""`.

### Missing or `null`? (for PATCH)

A `T?` field gives `null` for both. To know the difference, use `Maybe<T>`:

```dart
@Length(max: 500)
final Maybe<String?> bio; // default: const Maybe.missing()

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}
```

## Types

| Dart type | JSON | Query and form data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` | the same JSON type | text, converted |
| `DateTime` | an ISO 8601 string | the same |
| an `enum` | the name, like `"admin"` | the same |
| `RequestFile` | not allowed | a file part |
| a `@Dto` class | an object | bracket keys: `address[city]` |
| `List<T>` | an array | `tags=a&tags=b` or `tags[]=a` |
| `Map<String, T>` | an object | bracket keys: `meta[color]` |

JSON is strict: `"18"` is not an `int`. Query and form data are text, so Dox converts them.
Every detail is in [Types in detail](validation-rules.md#types-in-detail).

## Where the data comes from

| Request | Dox reads |
| --- | --- |
| `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` | the query string |
| `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` | the body (JSON, form or multipart) |

Dox reads **one** source. It never mixes the query and the body.
To choose the source yourself:

```dart
@Dto(source: Source.query) // on the DTO
class SearchUsers { ... }

await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query); // for one call
```

Path params are not part of a DTO. Ask for them as controller parameters, like `int id`.

## Keys

The input key is the field name in snake_case: `firstName` reads `first_name`.

```dart
final String firstName; // key: first_name

@Name('emailAddress')
final String email; // key: emailAddress
```

- `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` uses the field names as they are.
- Unknown keys are dropped. With `@Dto(strict: true)`, an unknown key is an error.

## Rules

Put rules on a field as annotations. They run from top to bottom. The first rule that fails gives the error.

```dart
@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;
```

| Kind | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `@Length`, `@MinLength`, `@MaxLength`, `@Email`, `@Url`, `@Uuid`, `@Ip`, `@Regex`, `@In`, `@NotIn`, `@StartsWith`, `@EndsWith`, `@Alpha`, `@AlphaNumeric`, `@AlphaDash` |
| Change text | `@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`, `@AllowEmpty` |
| Numbers | `@Min`, `@Max`, `@Range`, `@Positive`, `@GreaterThan`, `@LessThan`, `@In`, `@NotIn` |
| Lists | `@MinItems`, `@MaxItems`, `@UniqueItems` |
| Dates | `@After`, `@Before` |
| Files | `@MaxSize`, `@Mimes`, `@Image` |
| Database | `@Unique`, `@Exists` |

Every rule, with its error code and message, is in [Validation rules](validation-rules.md).

- A rule on a list checks each item: `@Email()` on a `List<String>`. Only the list rules check the list itself.
- For a few allowed values, use a Dart `enum`, or `@In(<String>['draft', 'published'])`.

## Nested objects and lists

A field can be another `@Dto` class, or a list of them.

```dart
@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}
```

`Address` and `OrderItem` are `@Dto` classes too. An error in a nested value has a path key, like `items.1.quantity`.

## Files

A `RequestFile` field reads a file from `multipart/form-data`.

```dart
@Image()
@MaxSize('2MB')
final RequestFile avatar;

@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
final List<RequestFile> documents;
```

Dox checks the real file type from its first bytes. It does not trust the file name or the client.
To save the file, see [File upload](../guides/file-upload.md).

## Checks across fields: `validate()`

Add a `validate(DtoErrors errors)` method to the DTO. Dox calls it after all field rules passed.

```dart
void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
  if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
    errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
  }
}
```

- The key is the input key (snake_case). Use `_root` for an error about the whole body.
- `errors.has(key)` tells you if a key already has an error.
- The method can be `async`. Do not throw for bad input. Add an error.

## Database rules: `@Unique` and `@Exists`

These read the database, so they run last.

```dart
@Unique('users', column: 'email')
final String email;

@Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
final int teamId;
```

For an update, skip the row you are updating with `ignoreParam`:

```dart
// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')
final String email;
```

All options are in [Validation rules: database](validation-rules.md#database).
The full order of checks is in [The order of checks](validation-rules.md#the-order-of-checks).

## The error response

When a check fails, Dox answers `422` with one message per field:

```json
{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}
```

The key is the path to the value, with the input keys. List items use the index.

## Messages

Change a message in one of these places. The first one wins.

1. On the rule: `@Email(message: 'Please check your email')`.
2. On the DTO, by code or by `key.code`:

```dart
@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})
```

3. For the whole app, with a `MessageResolver`. Use it for other languages:

```dart
class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts = <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code]; // locale from Accept-Language
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: AppMessages(),
  // ...
);
```

Placeholders: `{field}` (the last key), `{value}`, and rule values like `{min}` and `{max}`.

## Custom rules

Extend `Rule<T>`. `T` is the field type (or the item type, for a list).

```dart
class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug'; // the error code
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}

// use it
@Slug()
final String slug;
```

- A rule with values: add `final` fields and override `params`. They become placeholders.
- `context.lookup('other.key')` reads another input value.
- A rule that needs the database: extend `AsyncRule<T>` and write `checkAsync`.

## Dynamic input

When the shape is known only at runtime (like form fields from the database), use a fluent schema:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));
```

See [Fluent schemas](../packages/validation.md#fluent-schemas-for-dynamic-input). Use a DTO for everything else.

## Testing

A DTO is a normal Dart class. Make one directly to skip the checks:

```dart
CreateUser input = const CreateUser(name: 'Ann', email: 'ann@dox.dev');
```

To test the checks, use `safeValidateMap`. It never throws:

```dart
ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors['email'], 'The email is not a valid email');
```

- `validateMap` does the same, but returns the object or throws.
- `source: Source.query` reads the map like a query string. `params: {'id': '5'}` gives path params.
- `@Unique` and `@Exists` need a test database.


---

# Validation rules

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xthe-basic/validation-rules/

# Validation rules

This page lists every annotation you can put on a `@Dto` field. See [Validation](validation.md) for how DTOs work.

How to read the tables:

- **Code** is the error code. Use it in `@Dto(messages: ...)` and in a `MessageResolver`.
- **Message** is the default English text. `{field}` is the last key of the path.
- Every annotation also takes `message:`. It wins over every other message.
- All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
- On a `List<T>` field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

## Type errors

These have no annotation. They come from the field type.

| Code | When | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | a required field is missing, `null`, or `""` | `The {field} is required` |
| `string` | not a string | `The {field} must be a string` |
| `integer` | not a whole number | `The {field} must be an integer` |
| `numeric` | not a number (`double`, `num`) | `The {field} must be a number` |
| `boolean` | not a bool | `The {field} must be a boolean` |
| `date` | not an ISO 8601 date | `The {field} must be a date` |
| `in` | not a name of the enum | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` |
| `array` | not a list | `The {field} must be an array` |
| `object` | not an object (nested DTO, `Map`) | `The {field} must be an object` |
| `file` | not a file | `The {field} must be a file` |
| `unrecognized_keys` | unknown key, with `@Dto(strict: true)` | `The {field} field is not allowed` |

## Text

For `String` fields (and `List<String>` items).

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Length(min: 3, max: 50)` | `length_between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@Length(min: 6, max: 6)` | `length` | `The {field} must be exactly {length} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@MinLength(3)` | `min_length` | `The {field} must be at least {min} characters` | `minLength` |
| `@MaxLength(50)` | `max_length` | `The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters` | `maxLength` |
| `@Email()` | `email` | `The {field} is not a valid email` | `format: email` |
| `@Url()` | `url` | `The {field} must be a url` | `format: uri` |
| `@Uuid()` | `uuid` | `The {field} is invalid uuid` | `format: uuid` |
| `@Ip()` | `ip` | `The {field} must be an ip address` | `anyOf` `ipv4` / `ipv6` |
| `@Regex(r'[a-z]+')` | `regex` | `The {field} format is invalid` | `pattern` |
| `@In(['a', 'b'])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn(['root'])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |
| `@StartsWith('dox')` | `start_with` | `The {field} must start with {prefix}` | `pattern` |
| `@EndsWith('.dev')` | `end_with` | `The {field} must end with {suffix}` | `pattern` |
| `@Alpha()` | `alpha` | `The {field} must be an alphabetic` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaNumeric()` | `alpha_numeric` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic and number` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaDash()` | `alpha_dash` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic and dash` | `pattern` |

Details:

- `@Length` has `min:` and `max:`. Both are optional, but you must give one.
  With only `min:` it acts like `@MinLength`, with only `max:` like `@MaxLength`.
- Length counts characters (Unicode code points). `é` counts as 1.
- `@Url()` needs `http` or `https` and a host.
- `@Uuid()` takes any version. Upper or lower case.
- `@Regex(pattern, {message})` must match the **whole** value. You do not need `^` and `$`.
  The regex is checked when the generator runs. A bad regex stops the build.
- `@Alpha()`, `@AlphaNumeric()` and `@AlphaDash()` use ASCII letters `a-z`, `A-Z`. `@AlphaDash()` also allows `-` and `_`.
- `@In` and `@NotIn` compare exactly (case matters).

## Change text

These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order, wherever you put them:
`@Trim`, then `@Lowercase` or `@Uppercase`, then the "empty string is missing" check.

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Trim()` | removes spaces at the start and the end |
| `@Lowercase()` | makes the text lower case |
| `@Uppercase()` | makes the text upper case |
| `@AllowEmpty()` | keeps `""` as a value. Without it, `""` counts as missing. |

They have no error and no JSON Schema output. `@Lowercase()` and `@Uppercase()` together stop the build.

## Numbers

For `int`, `double` and `num` fields (and list items).

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Min(18)` | `min` | `The {field} must be greater than or equal {min}` | `minimum` |
| `@Max(100)` | `max` | `The {field} must be less than or equal {max}` | `maximum` |
| `@Range(1, 10)` | `between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max}` | `minimum`, `maximum` |
| `@Positive()` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than 0` | `exclusiveMinimum: 0` |
| `@GreaterThan(0.5)` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than {min}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMinimum` |
| `@LessThan(100)` | `less_than` | `The {field} must be less than {max}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMaximum` |
| `@In([1, 2, 3])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn([0])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |

The values are `num`. `@Min(1.5)` on an `int` field stops the build.

## Lists

For `List<T>` fields. These check the list, not the items.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MinItems(1)` | `min_items` | `The {field} must have at least {min} items` | `minItems` |
| `@MaxItems(5)` | `max_items` | `The {field} may not have more than {max} items` | `maxItems` |
| `@UniqueItems()` | `unique_items` | `The {field} must not have duplicate items` | `uniqueItems: true` |

`@UniqueItems()` works for `String`, numbers, `bool`, enums and `DateTime`. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

## Dates

For `DateTime` fields.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@After('2000-01-01')` | `after` | `The {field} must be a date after {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@Before('now')` | `before` | `The {field} must be a date before {date}` | `format: date-time` |

- The value is an ISO 8601 date, or `'now'` (the time of the request).
- Both are exclusive: `@After('2000-01-01')` does not accept `2000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
- To compare two fields (end after start), use [`validate()`](validation.md#checks-across-fields-validate).

## Files

For `RequestFile` and `List<RequestFile>` fields.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MaxSize('2MB')` | `max_size` | `The {field} may not be larger than {max}` | `maxLength` (bytes) |
| `@Mimes(['pdf', 'png'])` | `mimes` | `The {field} must be a file of type: {types}` | `contentMediaType` |
| `@Image()` | `image` | `The {field} must be an image` | `contentMediaType: image/*` |

- `@MaxSize` units: `B`, `KB`, `MB`, `GB`. `1KB` = 1024 bytes. A bad size text stops the build.
- `@Mimes` takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file.
  The file name extension must fit those bytes too. So `x.html` with GIF bytes does not pass.
  For types without a byte signature (like `txt` or `csv`), it uses the file name extension.
- `@Image()` is `@Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp'])`. No `svg`.
- The JSON Schema of a file is `{"type": "string", "format": "binary"}`, plus the keys above.

## Database

From `dox_orm`. Async: they run after all other checks passed.

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection})` | `unique` | `The {field} has already been taken` |
| `@Exists(table, {column, connection})` | `exists` | `The selected {field} is invalid` |

- `@Unique` column default: the input key. `@Exists` column default: `id`.
- `ignoreParam: 'id'` skips the row where `ignoreColumn` (default `id`) equals the path param `{id}`.
- They add nothing to the JSON Schema.

See [Database rules](validation.md#database-rules-unique-and-exists).

## Keys and DTO options

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Name('emailAddress')` | the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake_case. |
| `@Dto()` | marks the class. |
| `@Dto(source: Source.query)` | where to read: `Source.auto` (default), `Source.query`, `Source.body`. |
| `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` | keys: `KeyCase.snake` (default) or `KeyCase.field` (the Dart name as is). |
| `@Dto(strict: true)` | unknown keys are errors. Default `false`: they are dropped. |
| `@Dto(messages: {...})` | messages by `code` or `key.code`. |

A `///` doc comment on a field becomes its `description` in the JSON Schema.

## Types in detail

How each field type reads input. The short table is in [Types](validation.md#types).

- **JSON is strict.** In a JSON body, `"18"` is not an `int`. You get the error `integer`.
- **Query and form data are text.** Dox turns the text into the field type first. If it can not, you get the type error.
- `int` takes `18` or `18.0`, never a fraction. `"4.5"` or `4.5` gives `integer`.
- `bool` in text takes `true`, `1`, `yes`, `on` and `false`, `0`, `no`, `off` (any case).
- `DateTime` takes `2024-01-31` or `2024-01-31T10:00:00Z`. A value without a time zone is read as UTC.
  The result is always UTC (`isUtc == true`). A number (timestamp) is not allowed.
- An `enum` matches the Dart name exactly. `"Admin"` does not match `Role.admin`. Custom wire values (like `"ADMIN"`) are not supported.
- `Object?`, `dynamic` and `Map<String, dynamic>` take any value. They are not checked.
- In query and form data, one value for a `List<T>` field gives a list with one item.
- In bracket keys, list indexes are sorted and packed: `items[3]` alone gives a list with one item.
- A list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives `422`.

## Body types

| Body | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `application/json` (or any `+json` type) | read with strict JSON types |
| `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data` | read as text, then converted |
| any other content type | `415 Unsupported Media Type` |
| JSON that is not valid | `400 Bad Request` |
| JSON that is not an object (like `[1, 2]`) | `422` with the key `_root` |

## The order of checks

1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (`@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`). Find missing required fields.
2. The field rules, top to bottom.
3. The `validate()` method (nested DTOs first, then the parent).
4. Async rules (`@Unique`, `@Exists`, your `AsyncRule`), one at a time, in field order.

Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors. So the database is never asked about input that is already wrong.

- Steps 1 and 2 run per DTO. So one answer can have a type error in `address` and a rule error in `items.1`.
- Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.
- A default value is not checked by the field rules. Async rules check the final value.

## What the generator checks

The build stops with a clear error when:

- a field is not `final`, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
- a field type is not supported (see [Types](validation.md#types)),
- a rule does not fit the field type (like `@Email()` on an `int`),
- a `Maybe<T>` field has no `const Maybe.missing()` default,
- two `@Dto` classes in the app have the same name,
- the class is generic, or extends another class (other than `Object`).


---

# Cache

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/cache/

# Cache

`Cache()` keeps data that is slow to make, so the next request can read it fast.

It runs on [`dox_cache`](../packages/cache.md), which is built into `dox_core`.

## Drivers

| Driver | Where the data is | Shared between isolates | Locks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | files in a folder (default `storage/cache`) | yes, on the same machine | no |
| `memory` | a map inside the isolate | no | yes |
| `redis` | a Redis server | yes, also between machines | yes |
| `null` | nowhere. It stores nothing | - | no |

!!! warning "Many isolates"
    Dox runs one isolate per CPU core. Each isolate has its own `memory` store.
    So a value you put in one isolate is missing in the others.
    Use `redis` when all isolates and servers must see the same data.

## Config

Without a config, Dox has a `file` store (the default) and a `memory` store.
To change the stores, make `lib/config/cache.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': env.redisHost,
      'port': env.redisPort,
      'prefix': 'app_cache:',
    },
  },
);
```

Redis needs two keys that a new project does not have yet. Add them to
`lib/config/env.dart` and run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  String get redisHost => '127.0.0.1';

  int get redisPort => 6379;
```

Then pass it to `AppConfig(cache: cache)` in `lib/config/app.dart`.
Each store is made once per isolate, the first time you use it.

### Store options

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | `path` (default `storage/cache`), `prefix` |
| `memory` | `max_size`: the most items. When it is full, the item that was used least recently is removed. No limit by default. Expired items are removed when read, and by a sweep every few thousand writes. Also `prefix`. |
| `redis` | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default `6379`), `username`, `password`, `db` (default `0`), `tls` (`true`/`false`), `pool_size` (default 10), `prefix` |

The default `prefix` is `dox_cache:`.
You rarely need `pool_size`: the cache sends no blocking commands, so each isolate uses about one Redis connection.

## Values are JSON

A value must be a JSON type: `Map`, `List`, `String`, `num`, `bool` or `null`.
A `Map` comes back as `Map<String, dynamic>`. A `List` comes back as `List<dynamic>`.

## Usage

```dart
// no duration: the value stays forever
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

await Cache().get('foo');             // 'bar', or null when missing
await Cache().get('foo', 'default');  // 'default' when missing
await Cache().has('foo');             // true
await Cache().forget('foo');          // remove one key
await Cache().forever('settings', <String, dynamic>{'theme': 'dark'});
await Cache().flush();                // remove all items of the store
```

### `remember`

`remember` reads the value from the cache. When it is missing, the function runs and its result is stored.

```dart
List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () => Post().all(),
);
```

`rememberForever(key, fn)` does the same with no expiry.

### `getRaw`

`getRaw` gives the stored JSON text as it is. Send it as a response with no decode and no encode:

```dart
String? json = await Cache().getRaw('posts');
if (json != null) {
  return response(json).contentType(ContentType.json);
}
```

A missing key gives `null`. A stored `String` comes back as JSON, with its quotes: `"bar"`.
The `memory` driver also keeps JSON text, so `get` decodes on every hit there too.

### Another store

`store(name)` uses a store from the config instead of the default store:

```dart
await Cache().store('redis').put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().store('memory').get('foo');
```

### Tags

Put items under a tag. Then you can remove only the items of that tag:

```dart
await Cache().tag('users').put('u1', 'Ann');
await Cache().tag('users').flush(); // removes only the items of this tag
```

`tags(['a', 'b'])` uses many tags.

### Locks

A lock makes sure only one request (or one server) runs some code at a time.
The `memory` and `redis` stores support locks. Use `redis` when many isolates must share the lock.

```dart
CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis').lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    await buildReport();
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}
```

- `get()` tries once. It is `true` when you got the lock.
- `block(Duration(seconds: 5))` tries again and again until the time is over.
- The lock is freed after its `ttl`, even if you never call `release()`.

### More methods

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `add(key, value, duration:)` | store only when the key is missing. `true` when it was stored |
| `pull(key)` | get the value and remove it |
| `increment(key, [by])` / `decrement(key, [by])` | change an integer. A missing key starts at 0 |
| `repository` | the `dox_cache` `CacheStore`, for everything else |

See [dox_cache](../packages/cache.md) for custom drivers.

## Tests

To use a memory store in tests, see [Testing](testing.md#test-the-cache).


---

# File Storage

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xdigging-deeper/file-storage/

# File Storage

`Storage()` saves and reads files on a disk: the local folder, AWS S3 (and R2, MinIO, Spaces), or memory.

It runs on [`dox_storage`](../packages/storage.md), which is built into `dox_core`.

```dart
Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('avatars', file);
  return <String, String>{'path': path}; // /avatars/<uuid>.png
});
```

## Config

Without a config, Dox has one disk: `local`, in the `storage` folder.
To add disks, make `lib/config/storage.dart`:

```dart title="lib/config/storage.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      'url': 'https://app.test/files', // for url() and signedUrl()
    },
    's3': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 's3',
      'bucket': env.awsBucket,
      'region': env.awsDefaultRegion,
      'key': env.awsAccessKeyId,
      'secret': env.awsSecretAccessKey,
      'endpoint': env.awsEndpoint, // R2, MinIO, Spaces
    },
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory'},
  },
);
```

The `s3` disk reads five keys that a new project does not have yet. Add them to
`lib/config/env.dart` and run `dart run build_runner build`. They are nullable,
so the app starts without them:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  String? get awsBucket;

  String get awsDefaultRegion => 'us-east-1';

  String? get awsAccessKeyId;

  String? get awsSecretAccessKey;

  /// R2, MinIO or Spaces. Null for AWS.
  String? get awsEndpoint;
```

Then pass it to `AppConfig(storage: storage)` in `lib/config/app.dart`.

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| `local` | `root` (default `storage`), `url`, `app_key` (default: your APP_KEY), `visibility` |
| `s3` | `bucket`, `region`, `key`, `secret`, `token`, `endpoint`, `path_style` (MinIO), `url` (CDN), `visibility`, `acl`, `batch_delete` |
| `memory` | none. For tests |

The `s3` disk needs `bucket`, `key` and `secret`. When one is missing, the first use of the disk throws an `ArgumentError` that names the setting.

## Functions

```dart
// save with a new uuid file name, returns '/images/<uuid>.png'
String path = await Storage().put('images', bytes, extension: 'png');
String path2 = await Storage().putRequestFile('images', file);

Uint8List? bytes = await Storage().get(path);  // null when missing
bool found = await Storage().exists(path);
await Storage().delete(path);

String url = await Storage().url(path);         // needs the disk `url` option
String signed = await Storage().signedUrl(path, expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10));

// another disk
await Storage().disk('s3').put('reports', bytes, extension: 'pdf');
```

`putRequestFile` on the local disk moves the upload temp file. It does not read it into memory.

`putRequestFile` and `file.store()` take the extension from the file name. When the bytes are a known format (png, jpg, pdf, zip, ...) that does not match the name, the extension of the bytes is used. So a png sent as `a.html` is saved as `.png` and is never served as a web page.

### `stream` and `download`

```dart
Route.get('/photo', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().stream(req.input('path'));    // shown in the browser
});

Route.get('/report', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().disk('s3').download('reports/2024.pdf'); // saved as a file
});
```

Both read the file as a stream, from any disk, with `Content-Length`.
A big file is never loaded into memory. A missing file answers `404`.

### Full disk API

`Storage().use('s3')` returns the `dox_storage` `Disk`: `copy`, `move`, `listAll`, `getMetaData`,
`putStream`, `setVisibility` and more. See [dox_storage](../packages/storage.md).

## Serve local signed URLs

```dart
// lib/routes/web.dart
Route.files('files');                    // GET /files/{key*}, signed URLs only
Route.files('public', signed: false);    // any file of the disk
Route.files('docs', disk: 'memory');     // another disk than the default
Route.files('uploads', download: true);  // every file is a download
```

An html, svg, xml or javascript file is always sent as a download in a sandbox, so its script does not run on your site.
Every file has `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

```dart
String url = await Storage().signedUrl('invoices/1.pdf'); // https://app.test/files/invoices/1.pdf?expires=...&signature=...
```

A missing, wrong or expired signature answers `403`.
Set the disk `url` option to the full URL of the route (`https://app.test/files`).

## Tests

To swap a disk with a memory disk in tests, see [Testing](testing.md#test-file-storage).

## Your own driver

Implement `DriverContract` from `package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart`. Register it in a [service](services.md), so every isolate has it:

```dart
Dox().storage.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver());
await Storage().disk('dropbox').put('notes', bytes, extension: 'txt');
```
