# Validation

`dox_validation` checks input and gives you typed Dart objects.
It has two parts:

1. **DTOs**: a class with `@Dto()` and rule annotations. A generator writes the checks. Use this for almost everything.
2. **Fluent schemas**: `v.object(...)`, like [Zod](https://zod.dev). Use it only when the shape is known at runtime.

Both give all errors at once, and a JSON Schema for [OpenAPI](openapi.md).

!!! tip "Built into Dox"
    `dox_core` uses `dox_validation` and exports it. `import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart'` is all you need.
    The guide is at [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md). Every rule is in the [rules reference](../the-basic/validation-rules.md).
    This page is about the package itself, and about using it outside Dox.

## Install (outside Dox)

```bash
dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner
```

```dart
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';
```

The DTO generator is in `dox_builder`. Run it with `dart run build_runner build`.
`@Unique` and `@Exists` are in `dox_orm`, not here.

## DTOs

```dart
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
```

The generator makes, for each `@Dto` class:

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `$CreateUserDto` | a `const` `DtoSchema<CreateUser>`: the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema |
| `lib/dtos.g.dart` | `const List<DtoSchema<Object>> dtos`: every DTO in `lib/`. Dox uses it to find DTOs by type. |

The `static const ... schema = $CreateUserDto;` line is how you reach the schema: `CreateUser.schema`.

## `DtoSchema<T>`

`DtoSchema<T>` is also a `Schema<T>`. So it works everywhere a schema works:
inside `v.object(...)`, `v.list(...)`, with OpenAPI, and as a `StandardSchema`.

| Member | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `Future<T> validateMap(Map<String, dynamic> input, {Source source = Source.body, Map<String, String> params = const {}, MessageResolver? messages, String? locale})` | all checks, then the object. Throws `ValidationException` with the errors. |
| `Future<ParseResult<T>> safeValidateMap(input, {source, params, messages, locale})` | the same, but never throws for bad input. `result.success`, `result.value`, `result.errors`. |
| `T fromMap(Map<String, dynamic> input)` | builds the object with **no checks**. Reads keys, converts JSON types, uses defaults. A wrong type throws a `TypeError`. Only for data you trust. |
| `Map<String, dynamic> toMap(T value)` | the object as a map with the input keys (snake_case). `DateTime` becomes an ISO 8601 string, an enum its name. |
| `Map<String, dynamic> toJsonSchema()` | JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). |
| `parse`, `safeParse`, `parseAsync`, `safeParseAsync` | the normal `Schema` methods, with `Source.body`. `parse` throws a `StateError` when the DTO has async rules. |
| `Type get type`, `String get name` | `CreateUser` and `'CreateUser'`. |

`source: Source.query` reads the map like a query string: text is converted to the field type.
`params` are path params, used by `@Unique(ignoreParam: ...)`.
`messages` and `locale` change the error text for this call. See [Messages](#messages).

```dart
ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}
```

| `ParseResult` member | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `success` | `true` when there are no errors |
| `value` | the result. `null` when `success` is `false` |
| `errors` | the first message for each field, like `{'user.email': '...'}` |
| `fieldErrors` | all messages for each field |
| `issues` | the full list of `ValidationIssue` objects, with code and path |

!!! note
    `dox_core` has its own `ValidationException` (the HTTP 422 one), so it does not export the one from `dox_validation`.
    In a Dox app, both answer `422` when thrown in a controller. In tests, prefer `safeValidateMap`.

### JSON Schema of a DTO

For the `CreateUser` from the [Validation guide](../the-basic/validation.md) (with `age` and `role`):

```dart
CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();
```

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateUser",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 50 },
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 },
    "role": { "type": "string", "enum": ["admin", "user"], "default": "user" }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}
```

- `required` lists the required fields only.
- A nullable field has `"type": [..., "null"]`. A default becomes `default`.
- A nested DTO goes in `$defs` under its class name, with a `$ref`. OpenAPI moves it to `components/schemas`.
- `@Dto(strict: true)` adds `"additionalProperties": false`.
- A `///` doc comment on a field becomes `description`.
- Each rule adds its keys. See the [rules reference](../the-basic/validation-rules.md).

## Fluent schemas (for dynamic input)

Use these when you only know the fields at runtime. The output is a `Map`, not a class.

```dart
final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
  'address': Address.schema, // a DTO inside a fluent schema
});

// throws ValidationException when the input is not valid
Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

// never throws for bad input
ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);
```

In a controller: `Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);`

!!! warning "Different defaults"
    Fluent schemas do not follow the DTO rules. A key is required unless you add `optional()`.
    `""` is a value, not "missing". Text is not converted, unless you use `v.coerce`.

### Schemas

| Schema | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| `v.string()` | `min`, `max`, `length`, `nonEmpty`, `email`, `url`, `uuid`, `ip`, `datetime`, `regex`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `includes`, `alpha`, `alphaDash`, `alphaNumeric`, `trim`, `toLowerCase`, `toUpperCase` |
| `v.int()`, `v.num()` | `min`, `max`, `gt`, `lt`, `positive`, `nonNegative`, `multipleOf` |
| `v.bool()` | |
| `v.date()` | `DateTime` only. `min`, `max` |
| `v.enumOf([...])`, `v.literal(x)` | |
| `v.list(item)` | `min`, `max`, `nonEmpty` |
| `v.object({...})` | `strict`, `passthrough`, `strip`, `pick`, `omit`, `extend`, `partial` |
| `v.map(values, keys: ...)` | any keys |
| `v.union([...])` | the first match wins |
| `v.any()`, `v.file()` | `file()` has `image` and `extensions` |

On every schema:

- `optional()`: the key may be missing. `null` is still an error.
- `nullable()`: the value may be `null`. The key must be there.
- `nullish()`: both.
- `defaultTo(x)`: the value when the key is missing. (`default` is a reserved word in Dart.)
- `transform(fn)`, `refine(fn)`, `refineAsync(fn)`, `superRefine(fn)`, `superRefineAsync(fn)`, `use(rule)`.
- `describe(text)`, `example(x)`: only used in the JSON Schema.

### Coercion

Query strings and form data are text. `v.coerce` turns text into the right type first.

```dart
v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'
```

### Checks across fields

```dart
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);
```

### Async checks

`refineAsync` runs a check that needs the database. Then use `parseAsync()` or `safeParseAsync()`.
`parse()` throws a `StateError` when a schema has async checks.

### Custom rules in a fluent schema

A `Rule<T>` class works in both worlds: as an annotation on a DTO, and with `use()` here.

```dart
v.string().min(3).use(const Slug());
```

See [Custom rules](../the-basic/validation.md#custom-rules) for how to write one.

## Messages

Each error has a code, like `required` or `min_length`.
Placeholders: `{field}`, `{value}`, and rule values like `{min}` and `{max}`.

```dart
// for the whole app (outside Dox; in Dox use AppConfig(validationMessages: ...))
MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
});

// for one call
createUser.safeParse(input, messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
}));
```

For other languages, extend `MessageResolver` and override `resolve()`.
See [Messages](../the-basic/validation.md#messages).

## Standard Schema

Every schema, and every `DtoSchema`, implements the [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) interface (`StandardSchema`).
Code that only needs to validate can accept any `StandardSchema`, from Dox or from another library.


---

# OpenAPI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xpackages/openapi/

# OpenAPI

This page shows how Dox makes OpenAPI 3.1 docs for your API, and how to change them.
You write no docs code. You get a [Scalar](https://github.com/scalar/scalar) docs page at `/docs`, plus `/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`.

The docs come from three places:

- **the routes**: method, path, path params, middleware (login),
- **the request classes**: a `@Dto` class,
- **the controllers**: the `///` comment, the arguments and the return type of each method.

## In a Dox app

### 1. Run the builder

```bash
dart run build_runner build      # or: dox build_runner:build
```

`dox_builder` reads your code and writes `lib/openapi.g.dart`.
Run it again after you change routes, controllers, request classes or models.
`dox build_runner:watch` does it for you while you work.

### 2. Pass the result to the config

```dart title="lib/config/openapi.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/openapi.g.dart';

OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  openApi: openApi,
  // ...
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `null` | `true` or `false` turns the docs routes on or off. `null`: on only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local` |
| `info` | `Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0')` | title and version of the API |
| `servers` | `[]` | base URLs, like `[Server('https://api.my.app')]` |
| `registry` | empty | `openApiRegistry` from `lib/openapi.g.dart` |
| `securitySchemes`, `securityByMiddleware` | `{}` | see [Login schemes](#login-schemes) |
| `ui` | `DocsUi.scalar` | the docs page: `DocsUi.scalar` or `DocsUi.swagger` |
| `scalar` | `ScalarOptions()` | see [The docs page](#the-docs-page) |
| `pageTitle` | `info.title` | title of the `/docs` page |

### 3. Open `/docs`

Start the app and open `http://localhost:3000/docs`.
In production the docs are off, unless you set `enabled: true`.
The document is built on the first `/docs` request, then kept.

### The docs page

The page loads Scalar from the jsDelivr CDN, at a fixed version, and reads `/openapi.json`.
Change the look with `scalar:`:

```dart
OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  pageTitle: 'Blog API docs',
  scalar: ScalarOptions(theme: ScalarTheme.purple, darkMode: true),
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `ScalarTheme.default_` | Color theme. Same names as Scalar: `moon`, `purple`, `deepSpace`, `saturn`, `kepler`, `mars` and more. |
| `darkMode` | `false` | Start in dark mode. The user can still switch. |
| `showDownloadButton` | `true` | Show the button that downloads the document. |
| `proxyUrl` | `null` | Send "Try it" requests through this proxy. Off by default, so requests go from the browser straight to your API. |

`pageTitle` and all options are escaped, so a value can not break the page.

To use Swagger UI instead, set `ui:`:

```dart
OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry, ui: DocsUi.swagger);
```

## What you write, what you get

A normal controller. There are no docs annotations here:

```dart
class BlogController {
  /// Get one blog
  ///
  /// Deleted blogs are not found.
  Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }

  /// Create a blog
  Future<Blog> store(CreateBlog body) async { ... }
}

// routes
Route.get<BlogController>('/blogs/{id}', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (BlogController c) => c.show]);
```

The generated docs for `GET /blogs/{id}`:

```yaml
get:
  tags: [Blog]
  summary: Get one blog
  description: Deleted blogs are not found.
  operationId: BlogController.show
  parameters:
    - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
  responses:
    "200":
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Blog"}
    "401": {description: Not logged in}
    "404": {description: Not found}
    "500": {description: Server error}
  security:
    - bearerAuth: []
```

`Blog` is in `components/schemas`, made from the model:

```yaml
Blog:
  type: object
  properties:
    id: {type: integer}
    title: {type: [string, "null"]}
    user: {anyOf: [{$ref: "#/components/schemas/User"}, {type: "null"}]}
    created_at: {type: [string, "null"], format: date-time}
```

## How each part is found

| Part of the docs | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| path, method | the live route table |
| path param types | the controller arguments after the first one, in order. `int id` gives `integer` |
| tags | the controller class name without `Controller` (`BlogController` gives `Blog`) |
| operationId | `Class.method`, for example `BlogController.show` |
| summary | the first line of the `///` comment |
| description | the rest of the `///` comment |
| request | see [Request](#request) below |
| 200 answer | the return type, see [Response](#response) below |
| `401` and `bearerAuth` | a middleware whose class name ends with `AuthMiddleware` |
| `404` | the path has a `{param}` |
| `422` | the route has a request class. The body is `{field: message}` |
| `500` | every route |

Routes that the builder does not know (for example inline closures) still get a basic entry.

### Request

The builder looks in this order. The first one wins.

1. `@Body(T)`, `@Query(T)` or `@Request(T)` on the method.
2. An argument whose type is a `@Dto` class: `store(CreateBlog body)`.
3. A `req.validate<T>()` call in the method, where `T` is a `@Dto` class.

For `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` the request is the JSON body.
For other methods each field is one query parameter.
`@Dto(source: Source.query)` or `Source.body` chooses the place by hand.
The route `body:` option still works, and it wins over all of these.

A `@Dto` class:

```dart
@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  final String title;

  /// Text of the blog.
  final String? description;   // nullable: optional

  final int views;             // default: optional, `default: 0`

  final Status status;         // enum: only `draft` or `published`

  final List<Tag> tags;        // a list of another @Dto class

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.description, this.views = 0,
      required this.status, required this.tags});
}
```

The keys are the same as the keys the DTO reads: snake_case by default (`postCode` is `post_code`),
or `@Name('key')`, or `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)`.
Each rule annotation adds its JSON Schema keys. See the [rules reference](../the-basic/validation-rules.md).

### Response

The return type of the method gives the `200` answer. `Future<T>` counts as `T`.

| Return type | Schema |
| --- | --- |
| a model (`@DoxModel`) | `$ref` to the model. Keys in `hidden` are left out |
| `List<Model>` | an array of the model |
| a `@Dto` class | `$ref` to the class |
| a `Serializer<Model>` | the map that `convert()` returns, else the model |
| `Pagination` | `total`, `per_page`, `last_page`, `current_page`, `data` |
| `String`, `int`, `bool`, `Map`, `List` | the basic JSON type |
| `dynamic` | the types of the `return` values. A map literal gives its keys. Exceptions are left out |
| `DoxResponse`, `void` | no schema |

A model schema has the primary key, the `@Column` fields, `created_at`, `updated_at`,
the relations (only there when loaded) and the `@Computed` getters.

## Change the docs (optional)

Add these to a controller method when the automatic result is not what you want.
They are all in `dox_core`.

```dart
@Summary('Log in')
@Description('Gives a bearer token for the Authorization header.')
@Tags(<String>['Auth'])
@Request(LoginUser)
@Response(200, LoginResult)
@Response(401, null, description: 'Wrong email or password')
Future<dynamic> login(DoxRequest req) async { ... }
```

| Annotation | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Summary('text')` | short title. Default: the first line of the `///` comment |
| `@Description('text')` | longer text. Default: the rest of the `///` comment |
| `@Tags(['Users'])` | groups. On a method or on the class |
| `@Request(T)` | the request class. Body or query by the HTTP method |
| `@Body(T)` | the request class, always the body |
| `@Query(T)` | the request class, always the query |
| `@Response(status, Type, description: '')` | one answer. Add more than one for more codes. With a `2xx` one, the return type is not used |
| `@ApiDeprecated()` | marks the route as deprecated. Dart `@Deprecated` works too |
| `@ApiIgnore()` | leaves the method (or the whole class) out of the docs |
| `@DoxController(tag: 'Users')` | for a class that the builder can not see in a `Route.get(...)` call |

The `Type` of `@Response` can be a model, `List<User>`, a `@Dto`, a `Serializer` or a basic type like `String`.

Each annotation also has a lower case name, like `@summary('Log in')`.
Only `@Response` has none, because `response()` is already a `dox_core` helper.

### Login schemes

A middleware whose class name ends with `AuthMiddleware` adds `bearerAuth` (a JWT bearer token) by itself.
For other middleware, or another scheme, set it in the config:

```dart
OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{
    'apiKey': SecurityScheme.apiKey(name: 'X-API-Key'),
  },
  securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
    'ApiKeyMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[
      <String, List<String>>{'apiKey': <String>[]},
    ],
  },
);
```

## How a route finds its docs

The builder saves the docs of each controller method, and each `Route.get(...)` / `Route.resource(...)` call it finds.
At runtime, Dox matches each route handler by its method name, HTTP method and the end of its path.
If there is no match, it picks the only method with that name and the same argument types.
Group prefixes (like `api/`) do not matter.

!!! tip
    If two controllers have a method with the same name, register the routes with
    `Route.get('path', controller.method)` so the builder can see them.

### Write the files: `dox openapi:generate`

```bash
dox openapi:generate              # storage/openapi/openapi.json and openapi.yaml
dox openapi:generate docs/api     # another folder
```

It runs `bin/openapi.dart` of your app:

```dart title="bin/openapi.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().writeOpenApi(args.isEmpty ? 'storage/openapi' : args.first);
  exit(0);
}
```

`writeOpenApi` runs your services and registers the routes. It does not start the server.

## Without Dox

`dox_openapi` also works on its own. Describe routes by hand with `ApiDoc`:

```dart
import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart';

ApiDoc docs = ApiDoc();
Map<String, dynamic> user = docs.schema('User', userSchema); // returns a $ref

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    summary: 'Get one user',
    tags: <String>['users'],
    params: <String, Object>{'id': <String, dynamic>{'type': 'integer'}},
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
      404: const ResponseDoc(description: 'Not found'),
    });

OpenApi api = OpenApi(info: const Info(title: 'My API', version: '1.0.0'), docs: docs);

api.toJson();                              // Map
api.toJsonString();                        // pretty JSON
api.toYaml();                              // YAML
await api.writeFiles('storage/openapi');   // openapi.json + openapi.yaml

// Serve the docs from your own server
OpenApiServer server = OpenApiServer(api); // Swagger UI: OpenApiServer(api, ui: DocsUi.swagger)
OpenApiResponse? page = server.handle('/docs'); // also '/openapi.json' and '/openapi.yaml'
if (page != null) {
  // send page.body with the header Content-Type: page.contentType
}
```

A schema can be a JSON Schema `Map`, a [`dox_validation`](validation.md) schema, or any object with `toJsonSchema()`.
Paths can use `{id}` or `:id`. Both become `{id}`.
`DoxRouteAdapter().addTo(docs, routes)` adds a basic entry for each route you did not describe.


---

# Storage

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xpackages/storage/

# Storage

This page shows how to save and read files with `dox_storage`.

`dox_storage` gives one API for files in many places: local disk, AWS S3 and S3-compatible services.

!!! tip "Built into Dox"
    `dox_core` uses `dox_storage` for [`Storage()`](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).
    In a Dox app, set the disks in `config/storage.dart` (a `StorageConfig`), and use `Storage()`.
    `Storage().use('s3')` gives the `Disk` of this page. `Route.files('files')` serves local signed URLs.
    This page is for the full `Disk` API and for using `dox_storage` outside Dox.

## Install

```bash
dart pub add dox_storage
```

```dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
```

## Drivers

| Driver | Use for | Signed download URL | Signed upload URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LocalDriver` | a folder on the server | Yes (HMAC with your app key) | No |
| `S3Driver` | AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, GCS (HMAC keys) | Yes (SigV4) | Yes (SigV4) |
| `MemoryDriver` | tests | fake URLs | fake URLs |

## Set up the disks

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

Map<String, String> env = Platform.environment;

DriveManager drive = DriveManager(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, DriverContract>{
    'local': LocalDriver(LocalDriverConfig(
      root: 'storage',
      urlBase: 'https://app.test/uploads',
      appKey: env['APP_KEY'], // signs local URLs
    )),
    's3': S3Driver(S3DriverConfig(
      bucket: 'my-bucket',
      region: 'us-east-1',
      accessKeyId: env['AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID']!,
      secretAccessKey: env['AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY']!,
    )),
  },
);

Disk disk = drive.use('s3'); // or drive.use() for the default disk
```

`use()` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` when no disk has that name.

## Use a disk

```dart
await disk.put('avatars/1.png', bytes); // String, List<int> or Stream<List<int>>
await disk.put('a.json', '{}', options: WriteOptions(contentType: 'application/json', visibility: Visibility.public));
await disk.putStream('videos/big.mp4', File('big.mp4').openRead());

Uint8List data = await disk.get('avatars/1.png');
String text = await disk.getString('notes/a.txt');
Stream<List<int>> stream = await disk.getStream('videos/big.mp4');
ObjectMetaData meta = await disk.getMetaData('avatars/1.png'); // size, contentType, lastModified, etag
bool found = await disk.exists('avatars/1.png');

await disk.copy('a.png', 'b.png');
await disk.move('b.png', 'c.png');
await disk.delete('c.png');
await disk.deleteAll('avatars'); // every file under this prefix

ListResult page = await disk.listAll('avatars', ListOptions(recursive: true, limit: 100));
// next page: ListOptions(paginationToken: page.paginationToken)

await disk.setVisibility('avatars/1.png', Visibility.public);
Visibility v = await disk.getVisibility('avatars/1.png');
```

### Save an upload

Stream the upload to the disk. The file is not loaded into memory.

```dart
Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String key = 'avatars/${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}.${file.extension}';
  await disk.putStream(key, file.stream());
  return <String, String>{'url': await disk.getUrl(key)};
});
```

!!! warning
    Do not use `file.filename` from the client as the key. A client can send any name.
    Make your own name, like above or with a uuid.

## URLs and signed URLs

```dart
String url = await disk.getUrl('avatars/1.png');

// a download link that works for 10 minutes
String signed = await disk.getSignedUrl('avatars/1.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10)));

// the browser can upload straight to S3 with this URL
String upload = await disk.getSignedUploadUrl('avatars/2.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(contentType: 'image/png'));
```

- `expiresIn` is 30 minutes when you do not set it.
- S3 signed URLs can live at most 7 days. This is an S3 rule.
- `contentDisposition` asks the server to send this header on download, like `attachment; filename="report.pdf"`.
- Set `urlBase` to serve public files from a CDN.

### Check a local signed URL

In a Dox app, `Route.files('files')` does this for you.

`LocalDriver.getSignedUrl` returns `<urlBase>/<key>?expires=...&signature=...`.
Check it in the route that serves the file:

```dart
LocalDriver local = LocalDriver(localConfig);
bool ok = local.verifySignedUrl(keyFromPath, req.uri.queryParameters);
if (!ok) {
  return response('Forbidden').statusCode(403);
}
```

## S3-compatible services

### Cloudflare R2

Set `supportsAcl: false`. R2 does not take ACL headers.

```dart
S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
);
```

### MinIO

MinIO needs path style URLs, so set `forcePathStyle: true`.

```dart
S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'us-east-1',
  endpoint: 'http://localhost:9000',
  forcePathStyle: true,
  accessKeyId: 'minioadmin',
  secretAccessKey: 'minioadmin',
);
```

### DigitalOcean Spaces

Spaces works like S3. Put the region of your space in `region` and in the endpoint.

```dart
S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-space',
  region: 'nyc3',
  endpoint: 'https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
);
```

### Google Cloud Storage

Set `supportsAcl: false` and `supportsBatchDelete: false`. GCS does not take ACL headers or the S3 batch delete call.

```dart
S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://storage.googleapis.com',
  accessKeyId: 'GOOG...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
  supportsBatchDelete: false,
);
```

!!! info "Big files"
    - `put` sends one request. S3 allows at most 5 GiB in one request.
    - `putStream` uses a multipart upload when the stream is bigger than `multipartPartSize` (8 MiB).
      Only one part is in memory at a time. The limit is about 78 GiB. Raise `multipartPartSize` for bigger files.
    - `copy` and `move` copy on the server. S3 allows at most 5 GiB here.

## Keys are checked

- `a//b/./c.txt` becomes `a/b/c.txt`. `\` becomes `/`.
- `..`, absolute paths (`/etc/passwd`) and null bytes throw `InvalidKeyException`.
- `LocalDriver` also checks that the path stays inside its root folder.

## Errors

All errors extend `StorageException` and have the `key`.

| Error | When |
| --- | --- |
| `FileNotFoundException` | the file does not exist |
| `PermissionDeniedException` | file system permission error, or S3 403 |
| `InvalidKeyException` | unsafe key |
| `UnsupportedOperationException` | the driver can not do this |
| `DriverException` | anything else. The first error is in `cause` |

## Tests

`fake()` swaps a disk for a memory disk.

```dart
Disk fake = drive.fake('s3'); // drive.use('s3') now writes to memory
await uploadAvatar();         // your code
expect(await fake.exists('avatars/1.png'), isTrue);
drive.restore('s3');
```

## Your own driver

Implement `DriverContract` and register it.

```dart
class DropboxDriver implements DriverContract { ... }

drive.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver(...));
await drive.use('dropbox').put('a.txt', 'hello');
```


---

# Cache

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xpackages/cache/

# Cache

This page shows the full API of `dox_cache`, the cache behind `Cache()` in Dox.

It has `remember`, tags, atomic locks and four drivers.

!!! tip "Built into Dox"
    `dox_core` uses `dox_cache` for [`Cache()`](../digging-deeper/cache.md).
    In a Dox app, set the stores in `config/cache.dart` (the `CacheConfig` of this page), and use `Cache()`.
    `Dox().cache` is the `CacheManager`. `Cache().repository` is the `CacheStore`.
    This page is for the full API and for using `dox_cache` outside Dox.

## Install

```bash
dart pub add dox_cache
```

```dart
import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';
```

!!! note
    `dox_core` exports `CacheConfig`, `CacheManager`, `CacheStore` and `CacheLock` from this package.
    They are the same classes, so importing both packages is fine.

## Drivers

| Driver | What it is | Shared between isolates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memory` | a map in this isolate. Fast. Optional LRU size limit | No |
| `file` | one JSON file per key in a folder | Yes (same machine) |
| `redis` | Redis, with the [ioredis](https://pub.dev/packages/ioredis) package | Yes |
| `null` | stores nothing. Use it to turn caching off | - |

!!! warning
    Dox runs many isolates. Each isolate has its own `memory` cache.
    Use `redis` when isolates or servers must see the same data.

## Set up

```dart
CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app:'},
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store
```

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| every driver | `driver`, `prefix` (default `dox_cache:`) |
| `memory` | `max_size`: the most items. When full, the least recently used item is removed. No limit when not set |
| `file` | `path` (default `storage/cache`) |
| `redis` | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default `6379`), `username`, `password`, `db`, `tls`, `pool_size` |

`pool_size` is the most Redis connections one store opens in one isolate (default 10). A store uses about one, so you rarely change it.

## Basic use

```dart
await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));
await store.get('a');               // 1
await store.get('missing', 'none'); // 'none'
await store.has('a');               // true
await store.forget('a');
```

!!! info "No ttl means forever"
    `put` without a ttl keeps the value forever.
    A zero or negative ttl removes the key.
    `Cache()` in `dox_core` takes the ttl as a named argument: `Cache().put('a', 1, duration: Duration(minutes: 5))`.

## Remember

Get the cached value, or run the function and cache the result.

```dart
List<dynamic> posts = await store.remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 10), () async {
  return await loadPostsAsJson();
});
```

## All methods

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get(key, [default])` | the value, or the default when missing or expired |
| `getRaw(key)` | the stored JSON text, with no decode. Null when missing |
| `put(key, value, [ttl])` | store it |
| `add(key, value, [ttl])` | store only when missing. Returns true when stored |
| `has(key)` | true when the value is not null |
| `forget(key)` | remove it. Returns true when it was there |
| `flush()` | remove all items of this store |
| `many(keys)` / `putMany(map, [ttl])` | many keys at once |
| `increment(key, [by])` / `decrement(key, [by])` | change a number. A missing key starts at 0. The ttl stays |
| `forever(key, value)` | store without expiry |
| `remember(key, ttl, compute)` | see above |
| `rememberForever(key, compute)` | the same, without expiry |
| `pull(key, [default])` | get it, then remove it |
| `tags([...])` | a tagged view |
| `lock(name, [ttl, owner])` | an atomic lock |

## Values are JSON

Values must be JSON types: `Map`, `List`, `String`, `num`, `bool`, `null`. Other types throw.

- A `Map` comes back as `Map<String, dynamic>`. A `List` comes back as `List<dynamic>`.
- A stored `null` reads as a miss. `has` returns false for it.
- For a model, store `model.toJson()`, not the model.

## Tags

```dart
await store.tags(<String>['users']).put('u1', 'Ann');
await store.tags(<String>['users']).flush(); // removes only the 'users' items
```

Tags work with every driver. Old items are not deleted right away. They are just not found any more, and they go away when their ttl ends.

## Locks

Only one worker runs the code at a time.

```dart
CacheLock lock = store.lock('report', Duration(seconds: 10));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    // only one worker runs this
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}

bool got = await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5)); // wait up to 5 seconds
```

- `get()` takes the lock and returns `true`, or returns `false` when someone else has it.
- `block(timeout)` tries again every 50 ms until it gets the lock or the time is over.
- The `ttl` frees the lock by itself if the worker crashes. Without a ttl, the lock stays until `release()`.
- `release()` frees the lock only for the owner that took it.
- `memory` and `redis` support locks. The `memory` lock works inside one isolate only. `file` and `null` throw `UnsupportedError`.

## Prefix

Every store has a `prefix` (default `dox_cache:`). It is added to every key.
Use different prefixes when two apps share one Redis database.

!!! info "Redis `flush`"
    `flush` deletes only the keys with the prefix. It never runs `FLUSHDB`.
    An empty prefix makes `flush` throw.

## Your own driver

```dart
class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver()); // or add a ready driver
```

`MyDriver extends CacheDriver`. It must implement `prefix`, `get`, `put`, `add`, `increment`, `forget` and `flush`.
Override `lock` to support locks, and `close` to close its connections.

## Close

`cache.close()` closes the connections of every store that was built, eg. the Redis connections.
Memory, file and null stores have nothing to close. It is safe to call twice.
A store used after it is built again.

In a Dox app you do not call it. Dox closes `Cache()` stores on shutdown, in every isolate, after the open requests are done.


---

# Socket.IO

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xpackages/socketio/

# Socket.IO

This page shows how to run a Socket.IO server with `dox_socketio`, inside Dox or on its own.

`dox_socketio` is a Socket.IO v4 server for Dart.
The official clients connect to it with no changes: `socket.io-client` (JavaScript v4) and the Dart `socket_io_client` package.
It has acks, rooms, namespaces, binary data and long-polling.
Socket.IO is the way to do realtime in Dox.

## Install

```bash
dart pub add dox_socketio
```

## Quick start

```dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.on('connection', onConnection);
  await io.listen(3001);
}

void onConnection(Socket socket) {
  socket.emit('welcome', 'hello');
  socket.join('lobby');
  socket.on('chat', onChat);
}

void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
  event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data); // everyone in lobby but me
  event.ack('ok'); // answer the client callback
}
```

Client (JavaScript):

```js
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3001');
socket.emit('chat', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'ok'
```

## In a Dox app: same port as HTTP

`dox_core` can serve Socket.IO at `/socket.io/` on the app port. It is off by default.

`dox_core` does not export `dox_socketio`. Add it, and `ioredis` for the Redis adapter:

```bash
dart pub add dox_socketio ioredis
```

```dart title="lib/config/socketio.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));

SocketIoConfig socketIo = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace(MessageService())],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(), // shares broadcasts between isolates
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}
```

Add a getter for the `SOCKETIO_ENABLED` key to `lib/config/env.dart`, then run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  /// serve Socket.IO on the app port
  bool get socketioEnabled => false;
```

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  socketIo: socketIo,
  // ...
);
```

| `SocketIoConfig` option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `false` | serve Socket.IO at `options.path` |
| `options` | `ServerOptions()` | see [Options](#options) |
| `namespaces` | `[]` | `NamespaceHandler` classes to register |
| `adapter` | `null` (in-memory) | makes one adapter in each isolate |

- Requests to `/socket.io/` go to Socket.IO before the router. Middleware and body reading are skipped.
- When it is off, there is no extra work per request.
- `Dox().socketIo` is the server of this isolate: `Dox().socketIo?.to('room').emit('news', data)`.
- Need a plain WebSocket with no Socket.IO protocol? `Route.websocket(path, handler)` in `dox_core` gives you the raw socket.

!!! warning "Many isolates"
    Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server.

    - Clients should connect with **websocket only**. One websocket stays on one isolate.
      With the Redis adapter, a broadcast reaches clients on every isolate.
    - HTTP long-polling sends many requests, and they can reach different isolates. It only works
      with `totalIsolate: 1`, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.

    ```js
    const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });
    ```

    Dox logs this hint at startup when it runs many isolates and polling is allowed.

## Where to run it (outside Dox)

`io.listen(port)` opens its own port. Run it in its own small program, for example `bin/socket.dart`,
next to the Dox HTTP server. Put both behind the same proxy.

- `io.listen(port)` starts a native server (`dox_http_native`).
- `io.attach(httpServer)` uses a server you already have: a `NativeHttpServer` or a `dart:io` one.
- In your own server, call `io.handle(request)` when `io.matches(request)` is true.
- The path is `/socket.io/` by default.

## Namespaces in a class

A namespace can be a class. Its dependencies come in through the constructor.

```dart
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

  void checkToken(Socket socket) {
    if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
      throw SocketIoException('unauthorized', data: {'reason': 'bad token'});
    }
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

io.register(ChatNamespace(MessageService()));
```

When a middleware throws a `SocketIoException`, the client gets `connect_error` with the message and the data.
Any other error is written to stderr. The client only gets `{"message": "Internal error"}`, so it can not see private text like SQL.

A client that is refused is still closed after `connectTimeout`, unless it joins another namespace.

## Node.js to Dart

| Node.js | Dart |
| --- | --- |
| `socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...)` | `socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...)`, then `e.data`, `e.args`, `e.ack(x)` |
| `socket.emit('e', a, b)` | `socket.emit('e', a)` or `socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b])` |
| `await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a)` | `await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5))` |
| `socket.join(r)` / `socket.leave(r)` | the same |
| `socket.to(r).emit(...)` | the same |
| `socket.broadcast.emit(...)` | the same |
| `io.to(r).except(x).emit(...)` | the same |
| `io.of('/chat')`, `io.use(fn)` | the same |
| `socket.handshake` | `.headers`, `.query`, `.auth`, `.address` |
| `socket.data` | `socket.data` (a `Map`) |
| `io.in(r).fetchSockets()` | `io.to(r).fetchSockets()` (this server only) |

- `disconnecting` and `disconnect` give the reason in `event.data`, like `transport close` or `ping timeout`.
- Binary data: send a `Uint8List`. It can be anywhere in lists and maps.

## Options

```dart
SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: ['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(origins: ['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `/socket.io/` | the URL path |
| `pingInterval` | 25 s | how often the server sends a ping |
| `pingTimeout` | 20 s | how long to wait for the pong before the client is gone |
| `upgradeTimeout` | 10 s | how long an upgrade from polling to websocket may take |
| `connectTimeout` | 45 s | how long the client has to join a namespace |
| `maxHttpBufferSize` | 1,000,000 bytes | the biggest message. A bigger websocket message closes the connection |
| `transports` | `['polling', 'websocket']` | allowed transports |
| `allowUpgrades` | `true` | let polling clients move to websocket |
| `cors` | `null` | CORS headers for polling requests. It also checks the origin of websockets |

- `cors` with a list of origins: a websocket from another origin gets 403. A request with no `Origin` header (not a browser) is allowed.
- `cors: null`, or `*` in `origins`: websockets from any origin are allowed. If you log users in with cookies, list your origins.
- `*` together with `credentials: true` throws an `ArgumentError`. List your origins instead.
- Websocket compression is off. A message bigger than `maxHttpBufferSize` closes with code 1009.
- On a plain `dart:io` server (`io.attach`), the whole message is read before the size check. Also set a size limit in your proxy.

## Many servers: Redis adapter

With more than one server process, use the Redis adapter.
Then a broadcast on one server reaches the clients of all servers.

```dart
Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis),
);
```

- `Redis` comes from the `ioredis` package (`^2.0.0-alpha.3`).
- The subscriber needs its own connection. A Redis connection in subscribe mode can not run other commands.
- It uses the format of `@socket.io/redis-adapter`. Node.js servers with that adapter can share one Redis with Dox servers.
- It reads messages in msgpack and in JSON. It writes msgpack, like the Node.js adapter.
  If your Node.js servers use a JSON parser, set `format: RedisFormat.json`.
- Other servers can ask a Dox server for `fetchSockets`, `allRooms`, `socketsJoin`, `socketsLeave` and `disconnectSockets`. It answers.
- On a Dox server, `fetchSockets`, `socketsJoin`, `socketsLeave` and `disconnectSockets` only act on its own sockets.
  To act on all servers, use an [emitter](#emit-from-other-programs).
- Broadcast acks from other servers: Dox clients get the event, but their acks are not sent back.
- `serverSideEmit` from other servers is ignored.
- Long-polling needs sticky sessions, the same as with [many isolates](#in-a-dox-app-same-port-as-http). Or use `transports: ['websocket']` on the client.

## Emit from other programs

An emitter sends events to your clients without a Socket.IO server.
Use it in a queue worker, a cron job or a service in another language.
It writes to Redis, and every server with the Redis adapter sends the event to its clients.

Dart (for example in a Dox queue job or a CLI command):

```dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
  SocketIoEmitter emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

  await emitter.emit('news', {'title': 'hello'}); // all clients of `/`
  await emitter.to('room1').except('room2').emit('news', 'hi room1');
  await emitter.of('/chat').to('vip').emit('notice', 'for vip');

  await emitter.to('room1').socketsJoin('room3'); // sockets in room1 join room3
  await emitter.to('room3').socketsLeave('room1');
  await emitter.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

  await redis.disconnect();
}
```

Node.js, with [`@socket.io/redis-emitter`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@socket.io/redis-emitter):

```js
import { Emitter } from '@socket.io/redis-emitter';
import { createClient } from 'redis';

const redis = createClient({ url: 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379' });
await redis.connect();

const emitter = new Emitter(redis);
emitter.to('room1').emit('news', { title: 'hello' });
emitter.of('/chat').emit('notice', 'for everyone in /chat');
```

- The emitters of other languages (PHP, Python, Go) use the same format, so they work too.
- Binary data (`Uint8List` in Dart, `Buffer` in Node.js) arrives as binary.
- The emitter does not wait for an answer. It can not know if a client got the event.
- `key` must be the same as the `key` of the adapter. Both default to `socket.io`.


---

# Authentication

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xsecurity/authentication/

# Authentication

This page shows how to log users in with `dox_auth` and protect routes with a JWT token.

`dox_auth` checks an email and a password against your user table.
It gives back a JWT token.
The client sends this token in the `Authorization` header.
`AuthMiddleware` reads the token and loads the user from the database.

## Install

```bash
dart pub add dox_auth
```

A new app made with the `dox` CLI already has it.

## 1. Hide the password in the model

The token holds the user data as JSON, and anyone can read a JWT.
So the password hash must never be in `toJson()`.
Put it in `hidden`:

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users')
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}
```

## 2. Set up the auth service

```dart title="lib/services/auth_service.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

class AuthService implements DoxService {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'web',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'web': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

Dox finds the service by itself. Run `dart run build_runner build` and it is in `lib/container.g.dart`.

## 3. Add the routes

`AuthMiddleware` protects a route.
When the token is missing or not valid, the request stops with `401 Authentication failed`.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"

Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/register', (AuthController c) => c.register);
Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/login', (AuthController c) => c.login);
Route.get<AuthController>('/auth/user', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (AuthController c) => c.user]);
```

## 4. Write the controller

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class AuthController {
  /// Make an account and log in.
  Future<dynamic> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User();
    user.name = body.name;
    user.email = body.email;
    user.password = Hash.make(body.password);
    await user.save();

    String? token = Auth().login(user);
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': user};
  }

  /// Check the email and password. Give a token.
  Future<dynamic> login(LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth();
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// The logged in user.
  User? user(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }
}
```

`RegisterUser` and `LoginUser` are `@Dto` classes. See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md).

## 5. Send the token from the client

```http
GET /auth/user
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

## Read the user

After `AuthMiddleware`, `req.auth` holds the login.

| Code | What it gives |
| --- | --- |
| `req.auth` | an `IAuth?`. `null` when the route has no `AuthMiddleware` |
| `req.auth?.isLoggedIn()` | `true` when a user is loaded |
| `req.auth?.user<User>()` | the user model |
| `req.auth?.toJson()` | the user as a map, without `hidden` fields |

## The `Auth` class

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `Auth.initialize(AuthConfig)` | sets the config. Call it once, in a service |
| `Auth(guard: 'admin')` | uses another guard from `guards`. Without `guard`, it uses `defaultGuard` |
| `await Auth().attempt(credentials)` | finds the user and checks the password. Gives a token, or `null` |
| `Auth().login(user)` | gives a token for this user, with no password check |
| `user<T>()` | the user after `attempt` or `login` |
| `isLoggedIn()` | `true` when there is a user |

`attempt` searches only by the fields in `identifierFields`. It runs bcrypt also when no user is found, or when the user has no password, so the answer time does not tell whether an email has an account.
It returns `null` when the password is not a `String`, when no identifier is given, or when the password does not match.

## Options

### `AuthProvider`

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | required | a function that makes a new model, like `() => User()` |
| `identifierFields` | `['email']` | the fields `attempt` searches by |
| `passwordField` | `'password'` | the column with the bcrypt hash |

### `JwtAuthDriver`

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret` | required | the key that signs tokens, like `SecretKey(env.appKey)`. An empty key throws `ArgumentError`. A key shorter than 32 bytes also throws in production, and prints a warning in development, local and test. Make one with `dox key:generate` or `openssl rand -hex 32` |
| `algorithm` | `JWTAlgorithm.HS256` | the signing algorithm |
| `expiresIn` | `Duration(hours: 1)` | how long a token is valid |
| `issuer` | `null` | the `iss` claim. When set, `verifyToken` also checks it |
| `hashRounds` | `10` | the bcrypt cost of your stored hashes. Use the same value as `Hash.rounds` |
| `userCacheTtl` | `null` (off) | keep the user of a token in memory for this time. See below |

## More than one guard

Each guard has its own driver and its own user model.
For example, users and admins in two tables:

```dart
AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'web',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'web': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey)),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
    'admin': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey)),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => Admin()),
    ),
  },
);
```

Pick the guard by name:

```dart
String? token = await Auth(guard: 'admin').attempt(credentials);

Route.get<AdminController>('/admin', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(guard: 'admin'), (AdminController c) => c.index]);
```

The token keeps the guard name in its `aud` claim.
So a token from the `web` guard does not work on the `admin` guard, even with the same secret.
An unknown guard name throws an `ArgumentError`.

## Things to know

- **The token is not secret.** Anyone with the token can read `user.toJson()`. Keep private columns in `hidden`.
- **You can not cancel one token.** A token works until it expires. If you change the `secret` (your `APP_KEY`), all tokens stop working.
- **The user is loaded on each request**, by the id in the token. A deleted user can not log in, even with a valid token.
- **`userCacheTtl` skips that query.** With `Duration(seconds: 30)`, a deleted or changed user is seen only after 30 seconds. Each isolate has its own cache. Requests in that time share one user object, so do not change it per request.
- **Login does not block the server.** `attempt` runs bcrypt in another isolate.
- **Hash passwords** before you save them. See [Hashing](hashing.md).


---

# CORS

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xsecurity/cors/

# CORS

This page shows how to let a web page on another domain call your API.

A browser blocks a request from `https://my.app` to `https://api.my.app` by default.
The API must send CORS headers to allow it.
Dox adds these headers from `CORSConfig`.

## Set up

The config is in `lib/config/cors.dart`. Pass it to `AppConfig(cors: cors)`.

```dart title="lib/config/cors.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: true,
  origin: 'https://my.app',
  methods: <String>['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>['Content-Type', 'Authorization'],
  exposeHeaders: <String>['Content-Disposition'],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 600,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  cors: cors,
  // ...
);
```

## Options

Each option sets one response header.
An option that is `null` sends no header.

| Option | Header | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | - | `true` adds the headers to every route. Default: `true` |
| `origin` | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` | one origin, a `List<String>` of origins, or `'*'` for all |
| `methods` | `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` | a `List<String>` or a text like `'GET,POST'`. `'*'` allows all |
| `headers` | `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` | a `List<String>` or a text. `'*'` allows all |
| `exposeHeaders` | `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` | the response headers the page may read |
| `credentials` | `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` | `true` lets the browser send cookies |
| `maxAge` | `Access-Control-Max-Age` | how many seconds the browser keeps the preflight answer |

For `methods`, `headers` and `exposeHeaders`, a list is joined with commas.

## More than one origin

`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` accepts only one origin or `*`.
So when `origin` is a list, Dox checks the `Origin` header of the request:

- The origin is in the list: Dox sends back that one origin.
- The origin is not in the list: Dox sends no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header. The browser blocks the call.
- The list has `'*'`: Dox sends `*`.

With a list, Dox also sends `Vary: Origin`. This tells caches that the answer depends on the origin.

```dart
CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  origin: <String>['https://my.app', 'https://admin.my.app'],
);
```

!!! warning "`credentials` with `*`"
    Browsers do not send cookies when `origin` is `'*'`.
    When you need cookies, set `origin` to your real front-end URL.

## Preflight requests

Before some requests, the browser sends an `OPTIONS` request.
You do not need an `OPTIONS` route for this.
Dox answers it with `204 No Content` and the CORS headers.
It uses the CORS setting of the route that the browser asks about.

## Turn CORS on or off for some routes

`enabled` is the default for all routes.
Change it for a group of routes:

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
// CORS headers only on these routes (use with enabled: false)
Route.enabledCors(() {
  Route.get<PostController>('/public/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
});

// no CORS headers on these routes
Route.disabledCors(() {
  Route.post<WebhookController>('/webhooks/stripe', (WebhookController c) => c.handle);
});
```


---

# Encryption

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xsecurity/encryption/

# Encryption

This page shows how to encrypt and decrypt text with `AESEncryptor`.

Dox uses `AESEncryptor` to encrypt cookies with your `APP_KEY`.
You can also call it yourself.

## Encrypt and decrypt

```dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

String secret = env.appKey; // 32 characters

String encoded = AESEncryptor.encode('Hello world', secret);
String decoded = AESEncryptor.decode(encoded, secret); // 'Hello world'
```

- `encode` returns base64 text.
- The same text gives a different output each time.
- `decode` throws `DecryptException` when the text was changed, or the key is wrong. It is a `400 Bad Request` error.
- The secret must be 16, 24 or 32 bytes long (AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256). Another length makes `encode` throw.

Make a new 32-character `APP_KEY` with the CLI:

```bash
dox key:generate
```

## Cookies

`DoxCookie` encrypts its value with `APP_KEY` by default.
`req.cookie(key)` decrypts it.

```dart
return response().cookie(DoxCookie('theme', 'dark'));  // encrypted
DoxCookie('theme', 'dark', encrypt: false);             // plain text

String? theme = req.cookie('theme');                    // decrypted
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);      // as sent
```

`req.cookie(key)` returns `null` when the cookie was changed, was made with another `APP_KEY`, or was made for another cookie name.
The cookie name is bound to the encrypted value, so a value can not be copied from one cookie to another.

## How it works

`AESEncryptor` uses AES-GCM.

- Each message gets a new random 12-byte nonce.
- The output is base64 of `nonce + encrypted text + tag`.
- The 16-byte tag checks the message. If someone changes one byte, `decode` throws.

To store passwords, do not encrypt them. Hash them. See [Hashing](hashing.md).


---

# Hashing

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xsecurity/hashing/

# Hashing

This page shows how to hash passwords with `Hash` and check them later.

A hash is one-way. You can not turn it back into the password.
`Hash` uses bcrypt with a new random salt each time. It is in `package:dox_core/dox_core.dart`.

## Hash a password

Hash the password before you save it.

```dart
user.password = Hash.make(body.password);
await user.save();
```

The result looks like `$2a$10$...`. It holds the salt, so you only store this one string.
The same password gives a different hash each time.

## Check a password

```dart
bool ok = Hash.verify('secret', user.password!);
```

`Hash.verify(password, hashedPassword)` returns `true` when the password matches.
It returns `false` when the password does not match, or when `hashedPassword` is not a valid bcrypt hash (for example an empty string).

## Without blocking the server

`Hash.make` and `Hash.verify` block the request isolate while bcrypt runs.
In a request handler, use the async versions. They run bcrypt in another isolate.

```dart
user.password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
bool ok = await Hash.verifyAsync('secret', user.password!);
```

## Cost

`Hash.rounds` is the bcrypt cost for new hashes. The default is `10`. Each step up doubles the time.

```dart
Hash.rounds = 12;
String hash = Hash.make('secret', rounds: 12); // or per call
```

Old hashes keep their own cost, so they still verify.
If you change it, also set `hashRounds` on `JwtAuthDriver` to the same value. See [Authentication](authentication.md).

## With login

You do not need `Hash.verify` for normal login.
`Auth().attempt()` from `dox_auth` finds the user and checks the password with bcrypt.
See [Authentication](authentication.md).

## Things to know

- Never store or encrypt a plain password. Hash it.
- Never send the hash to the client. Put the column in the model `hidden` list.
- bcrypt is slow on purpose, so guessing is slow too. Do not hash in a loop on hot paths.


---

# Rate limiting

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xsecurity/rate-limiting/

# Rate limiting

`RateLimit` is a middleware that stops a client that sends too many requests.
Use it on login, sign up and other routes that bots like to hammer.

## Limit a route

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/login', <dynamic>[
  RateLimit(max: 5, per: Duration(minutes: 1)),
  (AuthController c) => c.login,
]);
```

Each client (by ip) can now send 5 login requests per minute. The 6th request gets:

```text
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 42
X-RateLimit-Limit: 5
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0

{"code":"too_many_requests","message":"Too Many Requests"}
```

- `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the client can try again.
- Every answer, also a normal one, has `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.
- The error goes through your `exceptionHandler` and `responseHandler`, like any other error. So it has the same JSON shape as your other errors.

The defaults are `max: 60` and `per: Duration(minutes: 1)`.

## Limit every route

Put it in `globalMiddleware`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    RateLimit(max: 120),
  ],
  // ...
);
```

## Count by API key, not by ip

`key` picks who is counted. The default is `req.ip()`.

```dart
RateLimit(
  max: 100,
  key: (DoxRequest req) => req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? req.ip(),
)
```

The key is any `String`, so you can also count by user id after your auth middleware.

!!! warning "Behind a proxy"
    Behind Caddy, nginx or a load balancer, every request comes from the proxy ip.
    Then all clients share one count. Add the proxy to `AppConfig.trustedProxies`, so `req.ip()` is the real client ip.
    See [App config](../reference/app-config.md).

## Two limits on the same key

Two `RateLimit` with the same `max` and `per` share one counter. Give one a `name` to keep them apart:

```dart
Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/login', <dynamic>[
  RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'login'),
  (AuthController c) => c.login,
]);
Route.post<AuthController>('/auth/register', <dynamic>[
  RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'register'),
  (AuthController c) => c.register,
]);
```

## Where the counts live

The counts are kept in the [cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md):

- When the default cache store is **Redis**, the counts are in Redis. All isolates and all servers share them. Use this in production.
- Else the counts are in **memory**. Each isolate has its own counts. With 4 isolates a client can send up to 4 x `max` requests.

To use one store by name, pass `store`:

```dart
RateLimit(max: 10, store: 'redis')
```

## How it counts

It is a fixed window. With `per: Duration(minutes: 1)` the count starts at 0 at the start of each minute.
So a client can send `max` requests at the end of one minute and `max` more at the start of the next.
That is fine for most apps. For a hard limit, use a smaller window.

## See also

- [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md)
- [Security headers](security-headers.md)
- [Production checklist](../reference/production-checklist.md)


---

# Security headers

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xsecurity/security-headers/

# Security headers

`SecurityHeaders` is a middleware that adds safe HTTP headers to every answer.
The browser reads them and blocks some common attacks, like showing your page in a frame on another site.

## Turn it on

Put it in `globalMiddleware`:

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const SecurityHeaders(),
  ],
  // ...
);
```

Every answer now has these headers:

| Header | Default value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` | The browser does not guess the file type. |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` | No site can show your page in a frame. |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` | Other sites only see your domain, not the full url. |
| `Permissions-Policy` | `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()` | The page can not use the camera, the microphone or the location. |
| `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` | `same-origin` | A page of another site that opens yours can not reach it. |
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` | The browser uses only https for one year. Sent only on https requests. |

`Content-Security-Policy` is off by default. A good policy depends on your pages.

## Change or turn off a header

Each header has an option. Give a new value to change it, or `null` to turn it off:

```dart
const SecurityHeaders(
  frameOptions: 'SAMEORIGIN', // allow frames from your own site
  permissionsPolicy: null, // do not send this header
  contentSecurityPolicy: "frame-ancestors 'none'",
  extra: <String, String>{'Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy': 'same-origin'},
)
```

| Option | Header |
| --- | --- |
| `contentTypeOptions` | `X-Content-Type-Options` |
| `frameOptions` | `X-Frame-Options` |
| `referrerPolicy` | `Referrer-Policy` |
| `permissionsPolicy` | `Permissions-Policy` |
| `crossOriginOpenerPolicy` | `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` |
| `strictTransportSecurity` | `Strict-Transport-Security` |
| `contentSecurityPolicy` | `Content-Security-Policy` |
| `extra` | any other headers, name to value |

## HSTS behind a proxy

Dox serves plain http. The https part is done by a proxy (Caddy, nginx, a load balancer).
Dox sends `Strict-Transport-Security` only when the request came in over https.
It knows that from the `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` header, and it only believes this header from a trusted proxy.
So add your proxy to `AppConfig.trustedProxies`:

```dart
AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1']);
```

Without it, Dox never sends HSTS. See [App config](../reference/app-config.md).

!!! note
    Middleware runs only for routes that exist. A `404` for an unknown url does not get these headers.

## See also

- [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md)
- [CORS](cors.md)
- [Rate limiting](rate-limiting.md)


---

# Guides

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/

# Guides

Each guide solves one job from start to end. Copy the files, run the commands, and check the result.
The reference pages explain each part in more detail. The guides link to them.

The code of all guides is in one app on GitHub: [examples/guides](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/tree/develop/examples/guides).
CI builds it and runs its tests on every push, so the code on these pages keeps working.

| Guide | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| [File upload](file-upload.md) | Accept an image, check its size and type, save it, return its URL. |
| [Pagination](pagination.md) | A list route with `page` and `per_page`, and the JSON shape it returns. |
| [JWT authentication](jwt-auth.md) | Register, log in, protect routes, read the user, log out. |
| [Custom errors](custom-errors.md) | Your own exception classes, one JSON shape for every error, logging. |
| [Background work](background-work.md) | Run work after the response, use another thread for CPU work, run a timer. |
| [Docker](docker.md) | A small production image with `dox build`, Postgres, env and a health check. |
| [Testing with a database](testing-with-database.md) | Tests on SQLite or a test Postgres, with migrations and cleanup. |
| [Static files and SPA](static-files.md) | Serve a folder or a single page app, with cache headers. |
| [CORS for a browser front-end](cors-for-spa.md) | The CORS setup that works with a React, Vue or Flutter web app. |
| [Environments](environments.md) | Dev, staging and production config, `.env` files, secrets and `APP_KEY`. |

All guides use the app that `dox create my_app` makes. The package name is `my_app`.
Change it to your own package name in the imports.

# File upload

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xguides/file-upload/

# File upload

Accept an image from a form, check its size and type, save it to a disk, and return its URL.

## What you need

- A Dox app (`dox create my_app`).
- `build_runner` for the DTO (a new app has it).

## 1. Set up the disk

Give the `local` disk a `url`. `Storage().url()` uses it to build the public URL of a file.

```dart title="lib/config/storage.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storage = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    /// uploads go to the `storage` folder.
    /// `url` is the public address of `Route.files('files', ...)`.
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      'url': '${env.appUrl}/files',
    },
  },
);
```

`APP_URL` is a new key. Add a getter for it to the `AppEnv` class:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  /// the public URL of this app, used in file links
  String get appUrl => 'http://localhost:3000';
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` to update `env.g.dart`.
Then add `APP_URL=http://localhost:3000` to your `.env`.

## 2. Write the DTO

The DTO checks the file before your controller runs.

```dart title="lib/app/http/dtos/upload_image.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'upload_image.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  /// jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp or bmp. Dox reads the first bytes of the
  /// file to find the real type. The file name is not trusted.
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}
```

For other file types, use `@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])` in place of `@Image()`.

## 3. Write the controller

`putRequestFile` moves the upload to the disk with a new UUID name. It does not read the file into memory.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/upload.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/dtos/upload_image.dto.dart';

@Inject()
class UploadController {
  /// POST /api/upload (multipart/form-data, field `image`)
  Future<Map<String, String>> store(UploadImage body) async {
    // saves the file as /images/<uuid>.<ext> on the default disk
    String path = await Storage().putRequestFile('images', body.image);
    String url = await Storage().url(path);
    return <String, String>{'path': path, 'url': url};
  }
}
```

!!! warning "Save the file before you return"
    A file bigger than 1 MB is written to a temp file while it arrives.
    Dox deletes that temp file when the response is sent.
    So call `putRequestFile`, `store` or `moveTo` inside the controller, not later.

## 4. Add the routes

One route takes the upload. `Route.files` serves the saved files at `GET /files/{key*}`.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/upload.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.post<UploadController>('/upload', (UploadController c) => c.store);
  }
}
```

```dart title="lib/routes/web.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    // GET /files/{key*}, any file of the default disk
    Route.files('files', signed: false);
  }
}
```

`signed: false` makes every file public. Leave it out to serve only signed URLs. Then use `Storage().signedUrl(path)` in place of `Storage().url(path)`.

## 5. Build and run

```bash
dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs
dox serve
```

Make sure `lib/config/app.dart` has `dtos: dtos` from `lib/dtos.g.dart`. See [Validation: setup](../the-basic/validation.md#setup).

## Check it

Upload a PNG:

```bash
curl -F image=@photo.png http://localhost:3000/api/upload
```

```json
{"path":"/images/074aa0d0-ce21-11f1-938a-57265e28c4a3.png","url":"http://localhost:3000/files/images/074aa0d0-ce21-11f1-938a-57265e28c4a3.png"}
```

Open the `url` in the browser. The image shows.

Upload a text file. You get `422`:

```bash
curl -F image=@notes.txt http://localhost:3000/api/upload
```

```json
{"image":"The image must be an image"}
```

Send no file at all. You get `422` with `{"image":"The image is required"}`.

## Bigger files

The default limit for a `multipart/form-data` body is 100 MB. Change it in `AppConfig(maxMultipartSize: ...)`.
Set the same limit in your proxy (`client_max_body_size` in nginx).

## See also

- [Request: form data](../the-basic/request.md#form-data-file) for `RequestFile`
- [Validation: files](../the-basic/validation.md#files) for `@Image`, `@Mimes`, `@MaxSize`
- [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md) for S3 and signed URLs
