# Request and response

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/request-and-response/

# Request and response

A compact list of the members of `DoxRequest` and `DoxResponse`.

Examples and explanations are on the [Request](../the-basic/request.md) and [Response](../the-basic/response.md) pages.

## `DoxRequest`

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/http/request/dox_request.dart`. It implements `IDoxRequest` from `dox_annotation`.
A middleware gets an `IDoxRequest`. A controller gets a `DoxRequest`. The members marked `IDoxRequest` are on both.

### Input

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `validate<T>({Source? source})` | `Future<T>` | The request checked with the DTO `T`. Throws the `422` `ValidationException` on bad input. Throws `StateError` when `T` is not in `AppConfig.dtos`. | no |
| `validateSchema<O>(Schema<O> schema)` | `Future<O>` | Query and body checked with a fluent `dox_validation` schema. | no |
| `all()` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Query and body together. Body wins on the same key. | yes |
| `only(List<String> keys)` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Only these keys from `all()`. A missing key gives `null`. | yes |
| `input(String key)` | `dynamic` | One value from `all()`. | yes |
| `has(String key)` | `bool` | `true` when the key is there and its text is not empty. | yes |
| `add(String key, dynamic value)` | `void` | Adds a value to `all()` and `body`. | yes |
| `merge(Map<String, dynamic> values)` | `void` | Adds many values to `all()` and `body`. | yes |
| `body` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The parsed body (JSON or form fields). Files are `RequestFile`. | no |
| `query` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The query string. | no |
| `param` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | The route params, like `{'id': '5'}`. | no |
| `pathParams` | `Map<String, String>` | The route params as text. `null` values are left out. | no |
| `requestBody` | `RequestBody` | The body as it was read, for DTOs. | no |
| `isJson()` | `bool` | The content type is JSON. | yes |
| `isFormData()` | `bool` | The content type is form data (`multipart/form-data` or urlencoded). | yes |
| `toJson()` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | `all()` with files replaced by their file name. Lets `jsonEncode(req)` work. | yes |

### Headers, cookies and client

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `header(String key)` | `String?` | One header. `null` when it is not there. | yes |
| `headers` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | Every header. Many values of one name are joined. | yes |
| `httpHeaders` | `HttpHeaders` | The `dart:io` headers object. | no |
| `contentType` | `ContentType?` | The parsed `Content-Type`. | yes |
| `cookie(String key, {bool decrypt = true})` | `String?` | One cookie. Decrypted with `appKey` unless `decrypt: false`. | yes |
| `ip()` | `String` | The client IP, or `unknown`. From `X-Forwarded-For` only behind a trusted proxy. | yes |
| `scheme()` | `String` | `http` or `https`. From `X-Forwarded-Proto` only behind a trusted proxy. | no |
| `isSecure()` | `bool` | `scheme()` is `https`. | no |
| `clientIp` | `String?` | The client IP, or `null`. | no |
| `userAgent()` | `String` | The `User-Agent` header, or `unknown`. | yes |
| `host()` | `String` | The `Host` header, or `unknown`. | yes |
| `origin()` | `String?` | The `Origin` header. | yes |
| `referer()` | `String?` | The `Referer` header. | yes |
| `locale` | `String?` | The first language of `Accept-Language`, like `th`. `null` when there is none or it is `*`. | no |
| `auth` | `IAuth?` | The auth object set by `AuthMiddleware`, or `null`. | yes |

### Route and raw request

| Member | Returns | What it gives | On `IDoxRequest` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `String` | The HTTP method in upper case. | yes |
| `uri` | `Uri` | The request URI. | yes |
| `route` | `RouteData` | The matched route. | no |
| `getRouteData()` | `RouteData` | Same as `route`. | yes |
| `getRouteIdentifier()` | `String` | base64 of `<method>|<domain><path>`. Useful as a cache or rate limit key. | yes |
| `httpRequest` | `HttpRequest` | The `dart:io` request. Use it for raw access. | yes |

## `DoxResponse`

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/http/response/dox_response.dart`.
Every setter returns the same `DoxResponse`, so calls chain.

| Member | Returns | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DoxResponse(dynamic content)` | `DoxResponse` | The constructor. `content` can be a `String`, number, `Map`, `List`, a JSON serializable object, a `Stream<List<int>>`, a `File`, a `StreamFile` or a `DownloadableFile`. |
| `response([dynamic content])` | `DoxResponse` | Top level helper. Same as `DoxResponse(content)`. |
| `statusCode(int code)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets the status. Default `200`. |
| `content(dynamic content)` | `DoxResponse` | Replaces the content. |
| `getContent()` | `dynamic` | The content as it was given. |
| `stream(Stream<List<int>> stream)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets a byte stream as content. |
| `contentType(ContentType type)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets `Content-Type`. A `File` without it gets the type from its extension. |
| `header(String key, dynamic value)` | `DoxResponse` | Adds one header. |
| `withHeaders(Map<String, dynamic> values)` | `DoxResponse` | Replaces every header set so far with this map. |
| `cookie(DoxCookie cookie, {bool setExpire = false})` | `DoxResponse` | Adds a `Set-Cookie` header. `setExpire: true` sends the cookie as expired, which removes it. |
| `cache(Duration duration)` | `DoxResponse` | Sets `Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>`. |
| `process(HttpRequest request)` | `dynamic` | Internal. Writes headers, status, cookies and the body. |

How the content is sent (`responseDataHandler` in `packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart`):

| Content | Sent as |
| --- | --- |
| `null` | an empty body |
| `String` | text, as it is |
| `Map`, `List`, number, `bool`, object with `toJson()` | JSON, `Content-Type: application/json` |
| `DateTime` | its ISO 8601 text |
| `File` | streamed, with `Content-Length`, `Accept-Ranges` and one `Range` supported |
| `StreamFile` | streamed with its content type |
| `DownloadableFile` | streamed with `Content-Disposition: attachment` |
| `Stream<List<int>>` | streamed chunk by chunk |
| `IHttpException` | its status and `toResponse()`, see [HTTP exceptions](http-exceptions.md) |
| other `Exception` or `Error` | `500` with `toString()` as text |

A plain value returned from a controller (not a `DoxResponse`) is sent the same way. It only goes through a `DoxResponse` when `AppConfig.responseHandler` is set, or when it is a `File`, `StreamFile` or `DownloadableFile`.


---

# HTTP exceptions

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/http-exceptions/

# HTTP exceptions

An exception that extends `IHttpException` turns into an HTTP error answer.

You can `throw` it or `return` it from a middleware or a controller.

`IHttpException` is in `packages/dox-annotation/lib/src/core_annotation.dart`:

```dart
abstract class IHttpException {
  int code = 500;
  String errorCode = 'server_error';
  dynamic message = 'Server Error';

  dynamic toResponse() {
    if (message is Map) {
      return message;
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'code': errorCode, 'message': message.toString()};
  }
}
```

## The classes

Every class takes the named parameters `message`, `errorCode` and `code`. The table shows the defaults.

| Class | Package | Status `code` | `errorCode` | Default `message` | Dox throws it when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BadRequestException` | `dox_core` | `400` | `bad_request` | `Bad Request` | the body can not be read, like JSON that is not valid |
| `UnAuthorizedException` | `dox_auth` | `401` | `unauthorized` | `Authentication failed` | `AuthMiddleware` finds no valid token |
| `NotFoundHttpException` | `dox_core` | `404` | `not_found` | `Not Found` | a typed path param does not fit (`{id}` is not an `int`) |
| `PayloadTooLargeException` | `dox_core` | `413` | `payload_too_large` | `Payload Too Large` | the body is bigger than `maxBodySize` or `maxMultipartSize` |
| `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` | `dox_core` | `415` | `unsupported_media_type` | `Unsupported Media Type` | a DTO reads a body that is not JSON and not form data |
| `ValidationException` | `dox_core` | `422` | `validation_failed` | `{}` (a `Map`) | a DTO or `req.validate()` finds bad input |
| `InternalErrorException` | `dox_core` | `500` | `server_error` | `Server Error` | never by itself; for your own use |
| `QueryException` | `dox_core` | `500` | `sql_query_error` | `Error in sql query` | never by itself; for your own use |

Source files: `packages/dox-core/lib/exception/*.dart` and `packages/dox-auth/lib/src/auth_exception.dart`.

## What the client gets

`responseDataHandler` in `packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_response_handler.dart` sends the answer:

1. The status is set to `code`.
2. The body is `toResponse()`.
3. The body is sent as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`.

A text message gives a JSON body with the `errorCode` and the `message`:

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');
```

```
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}
```

A `Map` message is sent as it is, with no `code` key. `ValidationException` always has a map, one entry per field:

```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json

{"email":"The email is not a valid email","name":"The name is required"}
```

A request for a path that has no route answers like a `NotFoundHttpException` with the message `<METHOD> <path> not found`: `{"code":"not_found","message":"GET /nothing not found"}`. Your `responseHandler` gets it too, so you can change its shape.

To send your own JSON shape from one exception, pass a map:

```dart
throw NotFoundHttpException(
  message: <String, dynamic>{'error': 'not_found', 'message': 'Blog not found'},
);
```

Other errors: any `Exception` or `Error` that is not an `IHttpException` gets `500` with `{"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}`. When `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`, the body is `error.toString()` as text instead. It is also passed to the `report` method of the [exception handler](../the-basic/errors.md). An `IHttpException` is not reported.

A `ValidationException` from `dox_validation` (thrown by `schema.parse()` in a controller) is turned into the `422` `ValidationException` of `dox_core` with the same errors.

## Make your own

Extend `IHttpException` and set the three fields in the constructor:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({
    dynamic message = 'Forbidden',
    String errorCode = 'forbidden',
    int code = HttpStatus.forbidden,
  }) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }
}
```

Override `toResponse()` to give every error of your app the same JSON shape.

More examples are on the [Response](../the-basic/response.md#errors) page.


---

# Production checklist

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/production-checklist/

# Production checklist

Check each item before you deploy.

Items marked **Dox limit** are things Dox does not do for you. You must handle them outside Dox.

## Secrets and config

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_KEY` is set, 32 characters and secret | `dox key:generate`, or a random value of exactly 32 characters in the real env. It signs JWT tokens and encrypts cookies. Never use the value from `.env.example`. | [Encryption](../security/encryption.md) |
| `APP_ENV=production` | An empty `APP_KEY`, a key that is not exactly 32 characters, or an old sample key stops the app at start (`StateError`). Only `APP_ENV` `development`, `local` or `test` logs a warning instead. | [Env reference](env.md) |
| The env is complete | Run `dox env:check` in CI or before the deploy. It exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. | [CLI](cli.md) |
| No secrets in the image or in git | `.env` in `.dockerignore` and `.gitignore`. Pass values as env vars (`docker run -e`, `env_file:`, systemd `EnvironmentFile=`). `dox build` copies `.env.example` only. | [Docker](../guides/docker.md) |
| No comments after values in `.env` | The app strips `# note`, but migrations keep it in the value. Put comments on their own line. | [Env reference](env.md) |

## Auth and passwords

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JWT tokens expire | `JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn` is 1 hour by default. Pick a time that fits your app, like `JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey), expiresIn: Duration(hours: 12))`. | [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) |
| You can not revoke one token | **Dox limit.** There is no token list on the server. To log out everyone, change `APP_KEY`. | [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) |
| Passwords are hashed | `user.password = Hash.make(input)` (bcrypt). Never store or encrypt a plain password. | [Hashing](../security/hashing.md) |
| The hash is never sent | `List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];` in the user model. The JWT payload is `user.toJson()`, and anyone can read it. | [Authentication](../security/authentication.md) |
| Passwords have a max length | bcrypt throws on input over 72 bytes. Add `@MaxLength(72)` to the password field of the DTO. It counts characters, so non-ASCII text can still pass 72 bytes. | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) |

## HTTP and network

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTPS at the proxy | Dox has no TLS server. Run Caddy or nginx in front. Keep the app port private. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |
| `trustedProxies` is set behind a proxy | `AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'])`, or the proxy network, like `'172.16.0.0/12'`. Without it, `req.ip()` is the proxy and `req.scheme()` is `http`. Do not use `['*']` when the app port is public. | [App config](app-config.md) |
| Body limits are on | Keep `maxBodySize` (10 MB) and `maxMultipartSize` (100 MB), or lower them. Set the same limit in the proxy: `client_max_body_size 100m;` | [Request](../the-basic/request.md) |
| CORS has real origins | `CORSConfig(origin: 'https://my.app')`, or a list like `<String>['https://my.app', 'https://admin.my.app']`. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin when it is in the list. | [CORS](../security/cors.md) |
| No `credentials: true` with `origin: '*'` | The new project's `cors.dart` has `origin: '*'` and `credentials: true` with `enabled: false`. When you turn CORS on, set a real origin first. | [CORS](../security/cors.md) |
| Rate limiting | Add `RateLimit(...)` to login and other busy routes. Use a Redis cache store, so all servers share the counts. Or limit at the proxy, see [below](#rate-limit-at-the-proxy). | [Rate limiting](../security/rate-limiting.md) |
| Security headers | Add `const SecurityHeaders()` to `globalMiddleware`. | [Security headers](../security/security-headers.md) |
| gzip at the proxy | Keep `compress: false`. Turn on gzip in Caddy (`encode gzip`) or nginx (`gzip on;`). | [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md) |
| OpenAPI docs | Off in production by default (on only for `APP_ENV` `development` or `local`). Do not set `enabled: true` for a private API. | [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md) |

## Build and run

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AOT binary, not `dart run` | `dox build`, then run `build/bundle/bin/server`. Keep `bin/` and `lib/` together. Not `dart compile exe`. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |
| Native server loads | The app starts and the start line says `(native)`. When the library does not load, the app stops with `dox_http_native did not load` and the fix. | [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md) |
| Native database driver loads | The app starts and the database works. When the library does not load, the app stops with `dox_postgres_native did not load` (or `mysql`) and the fix. | [Postgres native](../database/postgres-native.md) |
| Isolates = cores | Keep the default `totalIsolate` (`Platform.numberOfProcessors`), or set `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` to the cores the container really gets. Use fewer when the database runs on the same machine. | [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md) |
| Shared state across isolates | Cache: `redis`, not `memory`. Socket.IO: a Redis adapter and `transports: ['websocket']`. | [Isolate](../digging-deeper/isolate.md) |
| A supervisor restarts the process | Docker `restart: unless-stopped`, or systemd `Restart=always`. Dox restarts a dead worker isolate, but not the main isolate. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |
| Writable temp folder | Uploads over 1 MB go to a temp file. A `FROM scratch` image needs `/tmp` with mode `1777`. | [Docker](../guides/docker.md) |
| Uploads live on a volume or S3 | The `local` disk writes to `storage/`. Mount it as a volume, or use the `s3` disk. | [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md) |

## Database

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Postgres or MySQL for a busy app | SQLite has one connection per isolate, and a query blocks the isolate. Use it for small apps only. With SQLite use an absolute file path, never `:memory:` with many isolates. | [Database](../database/index.md) |
| Migrations run once per deploy | The new project runs `Migrator(migrations: migrations).migrate()` in `bin/server.dart` before `startServer()`. Or run `dart run bin/migrate.dart run` (or `dox migrate`) in CI. Do one, not both at the same time on many machines. | [Migration](../database/migration.md) |
| Migrations use the right database | `dox_migration` reads `.env` and the real env. A real env var wins, but a key that is only in an old `.env` is still used. Do not ship a `.env` next to the binary, or give `Migrator(config: ...)` your own config. | [Migration](../database/migration.md) |
| Small MySQL migrations | MySQL saves `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `DROP` at once. A failed migration can leave half the changes. One table change per migration. | [Migration](../database/migration.md) |
| Pool size fits the database | `extra: {'maxConnectionCount': 10}`. The Postgres and MySQL drivers share one pool per process, so the total is the pool size, not isolates x pool size. Keep it under the database `max_connections`. | [Database](../database/index.md) |
| Query logging is off | `debug: true` prints every query. The new project's `database.dart` sets `debug` only when `APP_ENV=development`. | [Database](../database/index.md) |
| Backups | **Dox limit.** Dox has no backup tool. Use `pg_dump`, `mysqldump`, managed database snapshots, or a copy of the SQLite file (with the `-wal` file, or `sqlite3 app.db ".backup x.db"`). Test a restore. | |

## Logs and errors

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON logs | `LoggerConfig(enabled: true, prettyPrint: false)`. The new project sets `prettyPrint` only when `APP_ENV=development`. | [App config](app-config.md) |
| Log level | Set `LOG_LEVEL=warn` to print only warnings and errors. | [App config](app-config.md) |
| Access logs in one place | `LogMiddleware` writes one line per request, every 20 ms. A hard kill can lose the last lines. Turn it off when the proxy already logs requests. | [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md) |
| Errors go to your tracker | Extend `ExceptionHandler` and set `AppConfig.exceptionHandler`. Any non-HTTP error is passed to its `report` method. The client gets `500` with `server_error`. The error text is sent only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`. | [Error handling](../the-basic/errors.md) |

## Health and shutdown

| Check | How | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Health route | Add `Route.health('/health', checks: ...)` with a database check, so the load balancer knows when the app can not serve. | [Health check](../digging-deeper/health-check.md) |
| Graceful shutdown | On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, Dox stops taking connections and lets open requests finish, in every isolate. Set `shutdownTimeout` below the kill timeout of your platform. The `ORMService` closes the database in its `DoxShutdown` hook, and Dox closes the cache stores. Close your own connections in a `DoxShutdown` service. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#graceful-shutdown) |
| Zero downtime deploys | Run two processes (or machines) behind the proxy. Restart one at a time. | [Deployment](../digging-deeper/deployment.md) |

## Rate limit at the proxy

You can also limit at the proxy. Then bad clients never reach the app.

nginx:

```nginx
# in http { }
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;

# in server { location / { } }
limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
limit_req_status 429;
```

Caddy needs the [`caddy-ratelimit`](https://github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit) plugin (build Caddy with `xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit`):

```
example.com {
  rate_limit {
    zone api {
      key    {remote_host}
      events 100
      window 1m
    }
  }
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}
```

!!! note
    The proxy must see the real client IP. When there is a load balancer in front of the proxy, set the real IP module of the proxy first.


---

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/troubleshooting/

# Troubleshooting

Real problems, with the text you see, the cause and the fix.

The texts come from the source code.

## The native HTTP library did not load

**Symptom.** The app stops at start with this error:

```
Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>.
Fix: install Rust (cargo, see https://rustup.rs), then run the app again ...
```

At build time (`dart pub get`, `dox serve` or `dox build`) you may also see one of these:

```
dox_http_native: no native library for <os>-<arch>. Install Rust (cargo) to build it from source.
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext>: 404
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> failed: <error>
dox_http_native: sha256 of dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> does not match
dox_http_native: cargo build failed
```

**Cause.** The build hook of `dox_http_native` (`hook/build.dart` in [its repo](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-http-native)) tries, in this order: the `lib_path` user define, a local `native/target/release` build, the GitHub release download, and `cargo build`. None worked. Common reasons:

- No internet during `dart pub get`, or the release has no build for your OS and CPU (there are builds for macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64, Windows x64).
- Rust is not installed, so the fallback `cargo build` can not run.
- You compiled with `dart compile exe`. It does not run build hooks, so no native library is in the binary.
- The `<reason>` is `native library ABI <x>, expected <y>`: the library on disk is from another version of the package.

**Fix.** Pick one:

1. Install Rust with [rustup](https://rustup.rs) and run `dart pub get` again. The hook builds the library with `cargo`.
2. When the reason is an ABI mismatch and you set `lib_path`, rebuild that library: `cargo build --release` in the `native` folder of the `dox-http-native` repo.
3. Download the library from the GitHub release `v<version>` of [dartondox/dox-http-native](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-http-native/releases) yourself and point to it in the root `pubspec.yaml`:

    ```yaml
    hooks:
      user_defines:
        dox_http_native:
          lib_path: /path/to/libdox_http_native.so
    ```

4. Build with `dox build` (it runs `dart build cli`), not with `dart compile exe`.

The native database drivers find their library the same way. When it does not load, the app stops too, with:

```
dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>.
dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>.
```

The fix is the same as above, with the `dox-postgres-native` or `dox-mysql-native` repo.

See [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md), [Postgres native](../database/postgres-native.md) and [MySQL native](../database/mysql-native.md).

## Port already in use

**Symptom.** At start:

```
SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = 3000
```

`<code>` is `-1000` minus the OS error: `-1048` on macOS, `-1098` on Linux.

**Cause.** Another process listens on the port. Often it is an old `bin/server.dart` that `dox serve` did not stop, or a second copy of the app.

**Fix.** Find and stop the process, or use another port.

```bash
lsof -i :3000          # macOS and Linux: who has the port
kill <pid>
```

Or set `APP_PORT=3001` in `.env` (a new project reads it into `serverPort`).

## build_runner: conflicting outputs

**Symptom.** `dox build_runner:build`, `dox serve` or `dox build` stops with a build_runner message that starts with `Conflicting outputs were detected`, and names files like `lib/dtos.g.dart` or `lib/app/models/user/user.model.g.dart`.

**Cause.** The generated `.g.dart` files are on disk, but `.dart_tool/build` does not know them. This happens after a `git clone` with committed `.g.dart` files, after deleting `.dart_tool`, or after a Dart SDK update.

**Fix.** Delete the build cache and build again:

```bash
rm -rf .dart_tool/build
dart run build_runner build
```

If that is not enough, delete the named `.g.dart` files and build again. New build_runner versions have no `--delete-conflicting-outputs` flag, so the Dox CLI does not pass it.

## Ambiguous import: `Uuid`, `Name` or `Schema`

**Symptom.** The analyzer or the build says a name like `Uuid`, `Name`, `Range`, `Image` or `Schema` is an "ambiguous import".

**Cause.** `dox_core` exports the validation rule names (`Uuid`, `Name`, `Range`, `Image`, ...). Another import has a class with the same name, like `package:uuid`. `dox_orm` also has a `Schema` class.

**Fix.** Hide the name you do not use in that file:

```dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' hide Uuid;
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;
```

## A `.env` value with `#`

A `#` after a space starts a comment. The comment is not part of the value.

```ini
APP_PORT=3000 # dev port   -> 3000
DB_PASSWORD=abc#123        -> abc#123 (no space before the #)
DB_PASSWORD="abc # 123"    -> abc # 123 (quotes keep the #)
```

When a value must have ` #` in it (a space, then `#`), put the value in quotes. The quotes are removed.

## `Hash.verify` throws on a bad hash

**Symptom.**

```
Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length (The length should be greater than or equal to 28): "..."
```

or

```
Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt version: "..."
```

or, when the password is long:

```
Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long (The length should be less than or equal to 72): "..."
```

**Cause.** `Hash.verify(password, hash)` calls `BCrypt.checkpw` from the `bcrypt` package. It throws an `ArgumentError` when `hash` is not a bcrypt hash (it must start with `$2` and be at least 28 characters), for example when the column holds a plain password, an empty string or a hash from another algorithm. It also throws when the password is longer than 72 bytes.

**Fix.**

- Make sure every stored password went through `Hash.make()`. A plain password in the column is a bug in the code that saved it.
- Check the hash before you compare it, and treat a bad one as a failed login:

    ```dart
    bool ok = hash.startsWith(r'$2') && Hash.verify(password, hash);
    ```

- Refuse passwords longer than 72 bytes in your DTO, for example `@Length(max: 72)`.

For normal login use `Auth().attempt()` from `dox_auth`. See [Hashing](../security/hashing.md).

## MySQL 8 login fails

**Symptom.** The connection to MySQL 8 is refused at login, while the same user works from the `mysql` client. Often the user was made with the default `caching_sha2_password` plugin.

**Cause.** `caching_sha2_password` needs either TLS or the server RSA public key to send the password. A client that has neither can not log in.

**Fix.** The Dox MySQL driver (`dox_mysql_native`) supports `caching_sha2_password` (MySQL 8.4) and MariaDB 11. Check these settings on the connection in `lib/config/database.dart`:

| Setting | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Remote host without TLS | Turn on `useSSL: true`. |
| `useSSL: true` | The server must have TLS on. |
| `host`, `port`, `user`, `password` | A wrong value gives the same login error. `DB_PORT` is `3306` by default for MySQL. |

As a last resort, change the user on the server:

```sql
ALTER USER 'app'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY 'secret';
```

## SQLite: the database file

**Symptom.** An `SqliteException` with `unable to open database file`, or an empty database after `dox build`.

**Cause.** `database` is a file path. A relative path is relative to the folder you start the app from. `dox build` tells you to run `cd build/bundle && ./bin/server`, so `dox.sqlite` is then `build/bundle/dox.sqlite`. SQLite makes a missing file, but not a missing folder.

**Fix.**

- Use an absolute path, or make the folder first.
- Set it with `DB_NAME` (a new project reads it): `DB_NAME=/var/lib/my_app/dox.sqlite`.
- Migrations use `DB_DATABASE` or `DB_NAME` as the path too. Use the same value for both.

!!! warning "`:memory:` and isolates"
    `:memory:` opens a new empty database in each isolate. With `totalIsolate` above 1, every isolate sees different data. Use a file, or `totalIsolate: 1`.

Dox opens a file database with `journal_mode = WAL`, `synchronous = NORMAL`, `foreign_keys = ON` and `busy_timeout = 5000` (change it with `extra: {'busyTimeout': ...}`).

## `dox: command not found` after `dart pub global activate`

**Symptom.**

```
zsh: command not found: dox
```

right after `dart pub global activate dox ^3.0.0-alpha`.

**Cause.** `dart pub global activate` puts the `dox` script in `$HOME/.pub-cache/bin`. That folder is not in your `PATH`.

**Fix.** Add it to your shell profile and open a new terminal:

```bash
export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"
```

On Windows the folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Pub\Cache\bin`.

## Other startup errors

Short errors, like a bad route, a missing DTO or a bad env key, are in the [Error index](errors.md).


---

# Error index

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/errors/

# Error index

A lookup table of the messages Dox prints or throws. Search this page for the text you see.

- `<...>` is a part that changes, like a name or a number.
- Dart adds a prefix to some errors: `Bad state:` (`StateError`), `Invalid argument(s):` (`ArgumentError`), `Unsupported operation:` (`UnsupportedError`), `Exception:` (`Exception`).
- For problems that need a longer story, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

## dox_core: start of the app

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_KEY is not set. Run `dox key:generate` and put the key in .env` | `appKey` is empty. A warning, or a `StateError` that stops the app when `APP_ENV=production`. | Run `dox key:generate`, or set `APP_KEY` in the env. |
| `Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>. Fix: ...` | The native HTTP library is missing or from another version (`native library ABI <x>, expected <y>`). The app stops at start. | Do what the `Fix:` part says. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#the-native-http-library-did-not-load). |
| `Server started at http://<host>:<port> with <n> isolate (native)` | Normal start. `<host>` is the address it listens on: `[::]` means all interfaces. | Nothing. |
| `Windows: the native server runs on one isolate` | Windows has no `SO_REUSEPORT`. | Nothing. |
| `Socket.IO runs on <n> isolates: clients should use transports: ['websocket'] ...` | Socket.IO with more than one isolate and long-polling on. | Use a Redis adapter, and `transports: ['websocket']` in the client. |
| `[dox] isolate <n> error: <error>` | An error killed a worker isolate. The stack is on the next line. | Fix the error. Dox restarts the isolate. |
| `[dox] isolate <n> exited, restarting` | A worker isolate died. A new one starts after 1 second. | Look at the error line above it. |
| `SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>), port = <port>` | The port is in use. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#port-already-in-use). |

## dox_core: routes and controllers

These stop the app at start, so a bad route never reaches a request.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Route <where>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. Use DoxRequest, a @Dto class, a type from Route.bind, or String, int, double, num, bool for path params. ...` | A controller parameter has another type, the DTO is not in `AppConfig.dtos`, or there is no `Route.bind<T>` for a `{param}` of the route. | Change the type, add the binder, or run `dart run build_runner build` and set `dtos: dtos`. |
| `Route name "<name>" is used twice: <method> <path> and <method> <path>.` | Two routes have the same name. | Give one of them another name. |
| `Invalid argument (name): No route has this name: "<name>"` | `route()` or `Route.url()` with a name that no route has. | Check the name and the group `name:` prefix. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Route "<name>" (<path>) needs the param "<param>".` | `route()` without a value for a `{param}`. | Pass it in `params:`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Route "<name>" (<path>) has no param "<key>". ...` | `route()` with a param the path does not have. | Remove it, or pass it in `query:`. |
| `Bad state: No bound value of type <T> for the route param "<param>". ...` | `req.bound<T>()` for a param with no `Route.bind`, or of another type. | Add `Route.bind<T>('<param>', ...)`. |
| `Route <where>: the controller has more path params than the route has {...} params (<n>).` | The method asks for more path params than the path has. | Add the `{param}` to the path, or remove the parameter. |
| `Route <where>: a controller can have one @Dto only.` | Two DTO parameters. | Merge them into one DTO. |
| `Route <where>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones (<type>).` | Named or `[optional]` parameters. | Use positional parameters. Use `int?` with `{id?}` for an optional param. |
| `Route <where>: a controller can not be generic.` | The handler has type parameters. | Remove them. |
| `Route <where>: can not read the controller type <type>.` | Dox can not read the function type of the handler. | Use a plain method or function. |

## dox_core: env

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EnvException: the env is not valid` then `  - <KEY> is missing` | `AppEnv.load()` found a required key with no value. | Set the key, or give the getter a default. |
| `  - <KEY> must be <type>, not "<value>"` | A value does not fit the getter type. | Fix the value. Check for a `# comment` after it. |
| `Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default` | `Env.get<int>()`, `<num>`, `<double>` or `<bool>` with no value and no default. | Set the key, or pass a default. |
| `Env key "<KEY>" is not a valid <type>: "<value>"` | `Env.get<int>()` (or another type) got text that is not that type. | Fix the value. |

See [Environment variables](../digging-deeper/env.md).

## dox_core: requests (what the client gets)

An `IHttpException` with a text message answers `{"code":"<errorCode>","message":"<text>"}`.
The table shows the `message` text.

| Status | Message | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `404` | `<METHOD> <path> not found` | No route matches. | Check the method, the path and the router `prefix`. |
| `404` | `Not Found` | A typed path param does not fit, like `abc` for `int id`. | Send a valid value. |
| `400` | `The body is not valid JSON` | A DTO reads a JSON body that does not parse. | Send valid JSON. |
| `400` | `The form body is not valid` | A urlencoded body that can not be decoded. | Fix the client encoding. |
| `415` | `Unsupported Media Type` | A DTO reads a body that is not JSON or form data. | Send `Content-Type: application/json` or form data. |
| `413` | `Payload Too Large` | The body is bigger than `maxBodySize` or `maxMultipartSize`. | Send less, or raise the limit. |
| `422` | `{"_root":"The input has too many items (max 1000) or levels (max 10)"}` | Form or query keys with more than 1000 list items or 10 levels. | Send less nested data. |
| `422` | `{"<field>":"<message>"}` | A DTO check failed. | See [Validation rules](../the-basic/validation-rules.md). |
| `431` | (no text) | Native server: request line plus headers over 16 KB. | Send smaller headers or cookies. |
| `500` | `Server Error`, code `server_error`. When `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`, the body is `<error>.toString()` as plain text. | Any error that is not an `IHttpException`. It also goes to the `report` method of the `ExceptionHandler`. | Look at the server log. |

## dox_core: DTOs, storage and config

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bad state: <T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, run `dart run build_runner build` and set `dtos: dtos` (lib/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig.` | `req.validate<T>()` can not find `T`. | Do what the text says. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>"` | A disk in `StorageConfig` has a `driver` other than `local`, `s3` or `memory`. | Fix the driver name. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" needs the "<setting>" setting. It is missing or empty.` | An `s3` disk without `bucket`, `key` or `secret`, on its first use. | Set `AWS_BUCKET`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): invalid file` | `Storage().put()` with no `extension:`, and Dox can not find the type from the bytes. | Pass `extension: 'pdf'`. |
| `403` `invalid or expired signature` | A `Route.files()` URL without a valid `signature`, or after `expires`. | Make a new link with `Storage().signedUrl()`. |
| `404` `file not found` | `Storage().stream()` or `download()` of a missing file. | Check the path. |
| `Invalid argument (trustedProxies): not an ip or cidr: "<value>"` | A bad entry in `AppConfig.trustedProxies`. | Use an IP, a CIDR like `10.0.0.0/8`, or `*`. |
| `Invalid argument (type): must be asc or desc: "<value>"` | `orderBy(column, type)` with another direction. | Use `asc` or `desc`. |
| `400` `decrypt_failed` | `AESEncryptor.decode` got changed text or a wrong key. It throws `DecryptException`. `req.cookie()` catches it and returns `null`. | Check the key. For a cookie, ask the user to log in again. |

## dox_auth

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` `Authentication failed` | `AuthMiddleware` finds no token, a bad or expired token, or the user is deleted. | Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Log in again. |
| `Invalid argument(s) (salt): Invalid salt length ...` | `Hash.verify()` with a value that is not a bcrypt hash. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#hashverify-throws-on-a-bad-hash). |
| `Invalid argument(s) (password): Password is too long ...` | bcrypt with a password over 72 bytes. | Limit the length in the DTO. |

`Auth().attempt()` returns `null` for a wrong password. It does not throw. See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

## dox_orm

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Unsupported operation: dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to Postgres. Fix: ...` | The native Postgres library did not load. The app stops. | Follow the fix in the message. See [Postgres native](../database/postgres-native.md#when-the-library-does-not-load). |
| `Unsupported operation: dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to MySQL. Fix: ...` | The native MySQL library did not load. The app stops. | Follow the fix in the message. See [MySQL native](../database/mysql-native.md#when-the-library-does-not-load). |
| `PgServerException(<code>): <message>` | The Postgres server said no, eg. code `23505` for a unique violation. | Read `code`, `detail` and `constraint` on the exception. |
| `MysqlException(<code>, <sqlState>): <message>` | An error from MySQL, eg. code `1062` for a duplicate key. | Read `code` and `sqlState` on the exception. |
| `Exception: <name> not found` | `DatabaseConfig.connection` (or `withConnection()`) names a connection that is not in `connections`. | Fix `DB_CONNECTION` or the map. |
| `Exception: Invalid driver or not supported` | A `ConnectionConfig.driver` Dox can not open. | Use `Driver.postgres`, `Driver.mysql` or `Driver.sqlite`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): dox_postgres_native: bad connection config` | The native driver can not read the connection values. | Check `host`, `port`, `user`, `database`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): dox_mysql_native: bad connection config` | Same, for MySQL. | Same. |
| `SqliteException` with `unable to open database file` | The SQLite folder does not exist. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#sqlite-the-database-file). |

## dox_orm: schema builder

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bad state: foreign key <name>: call on(table)` | `table.foreign('x').references('id')` with no `.on('table')`. | Add `.on('table')`, or use `foreignId('x').constrained()`. |
| `Unsupported operation: postgres: change() of an auto increment column is not supported` | `change()` on an `id()` or `increments()` column. | Write the `ALTER` by hand with `schema.driver.execute()`. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not add a primary key to an existing table` | `primary(...)` in `schema.table()` on SQLite. | Make the table again with the key in `schema.create()`. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has CHECK constraints` | A SQLite rebuild (`change()`, `foreign()`, `dropForeign()`) on a table with other `CHECK`s. | Make the new table by hand in the migration. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: can not rebuild <table>, it has generated columns` | Same, on a table with generated columns. | Same. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: table <table> not found` | A SQLite rebuild of a missing table. | Check the table name. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: column <table>.<column> not found` | `change()` or `renameColumn()` of a missing column on SQLite. | Check the column name. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: foreign key <names> not found` | `dropForeign()` of a key the table does not have. | Check the key name or columns. |
| `Bad state: sqlite: rebuild of <table> breaks foreign keys` | After the rebuild, rows point to missing parent rows. | Fix the data first. |
| `Unsupported operation: sqlite: change() rebuilds the table, it only runs on a database` | `table.toSql(SqliteGrammar())` with `change()`. | Run it on a database, not as text. |

## dox_migration

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Exception: Could not connect to database: <error>` | The migrator can not open the database. | Check `DATABASE_URL` or the `DB_*` values. A real env var wins over `.env`. |
| `Unknown migration command: <cmd> (use run, rollback, reset, refresh or status)` | `dart run bin/migrate.dart <cmd>` with another command. | Use one of the five. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count>` | `rollback` with a bad option. | Use `--step=2`. |
| `Bad state: Migration <name> is both a Dart and a .sql migration` | Two files with the same name in `db/migration`. | Rename or delete one. |
| `Bad state: foreign key check failed: <table> points to a missing <parent> row` | SQLite: a migration left a broken foreign key. | Fix the data in the migration. |
| `Migrating: <name>` / `Migrated: <name>` | Normal progress. | Nothing. |
| `Migrations are already up to date!` | Nothing to run. | Nothing. |
| `Nothing to rollback!` | No batch to undo. | Nothing. |
| `No migrations found.` | `status` with no migrations. | Check `db/migration`. |

See [Migration](../database/migration.md).

## dox_cache

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Invalid argument(s): Cache store "<name>" is not configured` | `Cache().store('<name>')` or `defaultStore` names a missing store. | Add the store to `CacheConfig.stores`, or fix `CACHE_STORE`. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Cache driver "<driver>" of store "<name>" is not supported` | A store has a `driver` other than `file`, `memory`, `redis` or `null`. | Fix the driver name. |
| `Unsupported operation: <Driver> does not support locks` | `lock()` on the `file` or `null` store. | Use the `memory` or `redis` store. |
| `Bad state: Cache value of "<key>" is not an integer` | `increment()` or `decrement()` on a value that is not an `int`. | Store an `int`, or `forget()` the key. |
| `Invalid argument(s): Cache value of "<key>" is bigger than <limit> bytes` | A Redis value is too big. | Store less, or use files or a database. |
| `Bad state: RedisDriver.flush needs a prefix. It will not delete the whole database.` | `flush()` on a Redis store with an empty `prefix`. | Set a `prefix`. |

See [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md).

## dox_storage

The text has the form `<Exception>: <message> (key: "<key>")`.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FileNotFoundException: File not found` | The file is not on the disk. | Check the path. `Storage()` paths start with `/`, `Disk` keys do not. |
| `PermissionDeniedException: Permission denied` | The OS (local) or S3 (`403`) refused it. | Check file rights, or the S3 key and bucket policy. |
| `InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: path traversal is not allowed` | A key with `..`. | Do not build keys from user input. |
| `InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: absolute paths are not allowed` | A `Disk` key that starts with `/` or a drive letter. | Remove the first `/`. |
| `InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: key is empty` | An empty key. | Pass a file name. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase is not configured` | `Storage().url()` on a local disk with no `url` option. | Set `url` on the disk. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase and appKey are needed for signed URLs` | `signedUrl()` on a local disk with no `url`, or no `APP_KEY`. | Set both. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: S3 signed URLs must expire within 1 second and 7 days` | `signedUrl()` on S3 with a bad `expiresIn`. | Use a time up to 7 days. |
| `UnsupportedOperationException: Disk "<name>" is not registered` | `Storage().disk('<name>')` with a missing disk. | Add the disk to `StorageConfig.disks`. |
| `DriverException: <S3 error>` | Any other S3 error (network, `500`, wrong bucket). | Read the S3 code in the text. |

See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

## dox_validation

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bad state: Schema has async rules. Use parseAsync() instead.` | `schema.parse()` on a schema with an async rule. | Use `await schema.parseAsync()`. |
| `Bad state: Rule "<name>" is async. Use parseAsync() instead.` | Same, for one `AsyncRule`. | Same. |
| `Bad state: This refine is async. Use parseAsync() instead.` | `refine()` with an async function and sync parse. | Same. |
| `Bad state: DTO <name> has an async validate(). Use parseAsync() instead.` | A DTO with `Future<void> validate()` checked with a sync call. | Use the async call, like `req.validate<T>()`. |
| `Bad state: No value: the key was missing. Check isPresent.` | `maybe.value` on a `Maybe<T>` that is missing. | Check `isPresent` first. |

See [dox_validation](../packages/validation.md).

## dox_builder (`build_runner`)

These stop `dart run build_runner build`.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `The @Dto class <Name> has problems:` then a `- ...` list | One or more lines below. | Fix each line. |
| `- The field <Class.field> must be final.` | A DTO field is not `final`. | Add `final`. |
| `- The field <Class.field> must be a `this.<field>` parameter of the unnamed constructor.` | The field is not set by the constructor. | Add `this.<field>` to the constructor. |
| `- A @Dto class needs an unnamed constructor.` | Only named constructors. | Add `const Name({...})`. |
| `- A @Dto class can not extend another class (<Parent>).` | The DTO extends a class. | Copy the fields in. |
| `- A @Dto class can not be generic.` | The DTO has type parameters. | Remove them. |
| `- The type <T> of <where> is not supported. Use a basic type, an enum, DateTime, RequestFile, a @Dto class, or a List or Map of them.` | Field type not supported. | Change the type. |
| `- @<Rule> does not fit the type <T> of <where>.` | A rule on the wrong type, like `@Email()` on an `int`. | Move the rule, or change the type. |
| `- @Length on <where> needs min:, max: or both.` | `@Length()` with no limit. | Add `min:` or `max:`. |
| `- The @Regex on <where> is not a valid regex: <reason>` | The pattern does not compile. | Fix the pattern. |
| `- @MaxSize on <where> needs a size like '2MB' (units B, KB, MB, GB), not "<text>".` | Bad size text. | Use `'2MB'`. |
| `- The Maybe field <where> needs the default `const Maybe.missing()`.` | A `Maybe<T>` field without that default. | Add it. |
| `- <where> can not have both @Lowercase and @Uppercase.` | Both on one field. | Keep one. |
| `- The validate method of <Name> must take one DtoErrors: `void validate(DtoErrors errors)`.` | Wrong `validate` signature. | Use that signature. |
| `Two @Dto classes are named <Name>: in <a> and <b>. Dox finds DTOs by name, so rename one.` | Two DTOs with the same class name. | Rename one. |
| `Env getter "<name>" has type <T>. Use String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, an enum or List<String>.` | A `@DoxEnv` getter with another type. | Change the type. |
| `@DoxModel can only be used on a class.` / `@DoxEnv can only be used on a class.` | The annotation is on something else. | Put it on a class. |
| `Conflicting outputs were detected ...` | `build_runner` cache is out of date. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#build_runner-conflicting-outputs). |

## Native libraries (build hooks)

Printed during `dart pub get`, `dox serve` or `dox build`. `<pkg>` is `dox_http_native`, `dox_postgres_native` or `dox_mysql_native`.

There is no fallback. When a library is missing, the app stops with the reason and the fix. `dox_http_native` stops at start. The database drivers stop when the ORM opens the database.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<pkg>: no native library for <os>-<arch>.` | No ready build for this OS and CPU. | Install Rust. |
| `<pkg>: download <file>: <status>` / `<pkg>: download <file> failed: <error>` | The GitHub download failed. | Check the network, then `dart pub get` again. |
| `<pkg>: sha256 of <file> does not match` | The downloaded file is not the expected one. | Delete `.dart_tool` and try again. |
| `<pkg>: cargo build failed` | The build from source failed. | Read the cargo output below it. |
| `Bad state: <pkg>: <path> does not exist` | The `lib_path` user define points to a missing file. | Fix the path in `pubspec.yaml`. |
| `Unsupported operation: dox_http_native can not detach the socket. Use NativeWebSocket.upgrade for a WebSocket.` | Code called `detachSocket()` on a response. Rust owns the socket. | For a WebSocket use `NativeWebSocket.upgrade(request)`. |

See [Native server](../digging-deeper/native-server.md).

## dox_socketio

Printed to stderr. The connection or the request fails, the app keeps running.

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox_socketio: handler error: <error>` | Your namespace handler threw. The stack follows. | Fix the handler. |
| `dox_socketio: request error: <error>` | A Socket.IO HTTP request failed. The client gets `500`. | Check the client version and transport. |
| `dox_socketio: redis publish failed: <error>` | The Redis adapter could not publish. | Check Redis. |
| `dox_socketio: bad redis message: <error>` | The Redis adapter got a message it can not read. | Check that every app on the channel runs the same version. |

## CLI

| Text | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Could not find a command. Run `dox help` for more information.` | `dox` with no command. | Run `dox help`. |
| `Could not find a command named "<name>". Run `dox help` for more information.` | Unknown command. | Check the spelling. |
| `Invalid number of arguments for command "<name>".` | Too few or too many arguments. | Run `dox help <name>`. |
| `Command "<name>" not found.` | `dox help <name>` with an unknown command. | Run `dox help`. |
| `<name> already exists` | A `create:*` file is already there. | Pick another name, or delete the file. |
| `Folder name "<name>" already exist` | `dox create` into a folder that exists. | Pick another name. |
| `Invalid option <x>, use -m or --migration` | `dox create:model` with another option. | Use `-m`. |
| `Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count>` | `dox migration:rollback` with another option. | Use `--step=2`. |
| `db/migration has Dart migrations, but bin/migrate.dart is missing. ...` | Dart migrations but no entry file. | Run `dox make:migration <name>` once. |
| `Skip <file>: no class that extends Migration.` | A Dart file in `db/migration` has no migration class. | Add `class X extends Migration`, or move the file. |
| `.env.example is missing.` | `dox env:generate` with no example file. | Make `.env.example`. |
| `lib/config/env.dart is already there. Delete it to make it again.` | `dox env:generate` again. | Delete the file, or edit it by hand. |
| `lib/config/env.dart is missing. Run `dox env:generate` first.` | `dox env:check` with no env class. | Run `dox env:generate`. |
| `pubspec.yaml has no name.` | `dox env:check` can not find the package name. | Add `name:` to `pubspec.yaml`. |
| `bin/openapi.dart is missing. Make it with: ...` | `dox openapi:generate` with no entry file. | Make `bin/openapi.dart`. See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md). |
| `zsh: command not found: dox` | `$HOME/.pub-cache/bin` is not in `PATH`. | See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#dox-command-not-found-after-dart-pub-global-activate). |

See [CLI](cli.md).

# Changelog

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/3.xreference/changelog/

# Changelog

What changed in each package, newest first. This page is made from the
`CHANGELOG.md` files in the repo when the docs are built.

## dox_annotation

### Unreleased

- New: `@Inject()`. Put it above a class and `dox_builder` adds the class to the Dox container. `@Inject(singleton: false)` makes a new instance each time.

### 3.0.0-alpha.8

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.7

- Breaking: `IDox`, `IDoxWebsocket` and `WebsocketEvent` are removed. They were only used by `dox_websocket`.

### 3.0.0-alpha.6

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.5

- New `timestamps` option on `@DoxModel`. `timestamps: false` turns off `created_at` and `updated_at`, like `$timestamps = false` in Laravel. `createdAt: null` or `updatedAt: null` turns off one of them.
- New `primaryKeyType` option on `@DoxModel`. Use `primaryKeyType: String` for a UUID key. The default is `int`.
- Fix: `IHttpException.toResponse()` now returns `{"code": errorCode, "message": message}` for a text message, so the client gets the `errorCode`. A `Map` message is returned as it is.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- OpenAPI annotations, all optional: `@Summary`, `@Description`, `@Tags`, `@Request`, `@Body`, `@Query`, `@Response`, `@ApiDeprecated`, `@ApiIgnore`, `@DoxController`. Lower case names work too (`@summary(...)`), except `@Response`.
- The DTO annotations (`@Dto`, `@Length`, `@Email`, ...) live in `dox_validation`. `dox_core` exports them.
- `IDoxRequest` has no `validate()` and no `processInputMapper()` any more. Use a DTO.
- Breaking (small): these names are exported by `dox_core` too. If a file also imports a package with a `Request` or `Response` class (like `package:http`) without a prefix, add a prefix to that import.
- New `@DoxEnv()` and `@EnvKey('X')` for the typed env class.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.

## dox_auth

### 3.0.0-alpha.8

- Security: a JWT secret (`SecretKey`) shorter than 32 bytes stops the app with an `ArgumentError` when `APP_ENV` is not `development`, `local` or `test`. In those envs it prints one warning line. Make a key with `dox key:generate` or `openssl rand -hex 32`.
- `Hash` now comes from `dox_core`. dox_auth had its own copy. `package:dox_auth/src/hash.dart` re-exports it. No change in behaviour. dox_auth now depends on dox_core.

### 3.0.0-alpha.7

- Perf: `attempt` runs bcrypt in another isolate (`Isolate.run`). Before, each login blocked the server isolate for the whole hash.
- Perf: the dummy hash for unknown users is made when the driver is created, in another isolate. Before, the first login paid for two hashes.
- New: `JwtAuthDriver(hashRounds: 10)`. Set it to the bcrypt cost of your stored hashes.
- New: `JwtAuthDriver(userCacheTtl: ...)`. Keeps the user of a token in memory for this time, so `verifyToken` does not run `find(id)` on every request. Off by default.
- Security: `JwtAuthDriver` throws `ArgumentError` when the `SecretKey` is empty. Before, an app with no `APP_KEY` signed tokens with an empty key, so anyone could make a token for any user.
- Security: `attempt` runs bcrypt also when no user is found, or when the user has no password. Before, an unknown email answered much faster than a wrong password, so the time told which emails have an account.

### 3.0.0-alpha.6

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.5

- Breaking: `JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn` is 1 hour by default. Before, it was `null`, and tokens never expired.
- New: named guards work. Use `Auth(guard: 'admin')` and `AuthMiddleware(guard: 'admin')`. Before, only `defaultGuard` was used.
- A token keeps its guard name in the `aud` claim. A token from one guard does not work on another guard.
- `verifyToken` checks the `iss` claim when `issuer` is set.
- Breaking: `AuthDriver` methods get the guard name as a new parameter. `AuthEngine().guard(name)` replaces `AuthEngine().driver` and `AuthEngine().provider`.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- `dart_jsonwebtoken` 3.4 (`pointycastle` 4).

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.
- Uses `dox_orm` (was `dox_query_builder`).
- `dart_jsonwebtoken` 3.

## dox_builder

### Unreleased

- New: `lib/container.g.dart` builder. It finds every `@Inject()` class, every class that extends `Router`, every class that implements `DoxService` and every `@DoxModel` in `lib/`. It writes `registerContainer(IocContainer c)`, which makes each class with its constructor. Constructor parameters come from the container by type. Optional parameters that the container can not give keep their default. Required nullable ones get `null`.
- The build stops with a clear message for a required parameter the container can not give, for a dependency cycle (it shows the chain, like `A -> B -> A`), and for an abstract or generic `@Inject()` class. Two classes with the same name work: every import has a prefix.
- OpenAPI: typed routes (`Route.get<C>(path, (C c) => c.method)`) and `Route.resource(path, ControllerClass)` are read too.
- Generates the query scopes: an extension with one method for each `@Scope()` method, and `globalScopes` for `@Scope(global: true)`.
- Generates the column casts: `fromMap()` and `columnsToMap()` use the `cast` of `@Column()`. `bool` and enum fields get a cast without `cast`.
- Run `dart run build_runner build` to get the new code.

### 3.0.0-alpha.8

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.7

- The generated `fromMap()` takes a `DateTime` from the driver as it is. It only parses a string.
- New generated `columnsToMap()` with the columns only. `convertToMap()` adds the relations to it.
- Models with no `beforeGet` hook get `readsRowDates => true`, so their rows skip the date to string step. A `beforeGet` hook still gets dates as strings.
- `tableColumns`, `preloadList`, `timestampsColumn` and the relation matchers are `const`, so no new list or map is made on each call.
- Run `dart run build_runner build` to get the new code.

### 3.0.0-alpha.6

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.5

- `@DoxModel(timestamps: false)` makes a model without `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. `createdAt: null` or `updatedAt: null` turns off only one.
- The primary key field has the type of `@DoxModel(primaryKeyType: ...)`. It was always `int?`. The default is still `int`. The OpenAPI model schema uses the same type.
- Fix: a preloaded relation with a two word name (like `userInfo`) was missing from `toJson()`. The generator looked for `user_info` in the preload list, but the list has `userInfo`.
- Fix: the OpenAPI route scanner now puts one `/` between a group and a route path, like the router does.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- New builder `dox_builder:openapi`. It writes `lib/openapi.g.dart` with the OpenAPI docs of the app: it reads the `Route.*` calls, the controllers, the `@Dto` classes and the models. It writes nothing when the package has no controllers.
- `DtoJsonSchema`, `ModelSchema` and `JsonSchemaReader`: the JSON Schema of a `@Dto` class, a model or any Dart type. Other builders can use them.
- New: the DTO generator. For each `@Dto` class it writes `$<Name>Dto` (a `const DtoSchema<Name>`) into the `.g.dart` part: plain `if` checks per field, the converter, `fromMap`, `toMap` and the JSON Schema. It stops the build with a clear error for a bad DTO (a field that is not final, a type that is not supported, a rule that does not fit, a bad regex, ...).
- New builder `dox_builder:dtos`. It writes `lib/dtos.g.dart` with every DTO of the app, for `AppConfig(dtos: dtos)`. Two DTOs with the same name stop the build.
- `DtoReader`: the one place that knows DTO keys. The OpenAPI docs use the same keys as the DTO (snake_case by default, `@Name`, `@Dto(keyCase:)`).
- OpenAPI: `@Regex` (was `@Pattern`). `@Format` is removed. Form requests are removed.
- Fix: the OpenAPI route list has the full path, with the `Router` prefix and `Route.group()` prefixes. Two `'/'` routes in two groups now each get their docs.
- OpenAPI path params: every positional argument that is not the request and not a DTO.
- New: `@DoxEnv()` classes get `_$<Class>` in the `.g.dart` part. Each getter is read from the env once, converted to its type (String, int, double, num, bool, Uri, Duration, enum, List<String>) and kept in a final field. A getter body is the default. A nullable getter is optional. `load()` throws one `EnvException` with every missing or bad key.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
- See the [release notes](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/pull/112) for all main changes.
- Works with analyzer 5 and 6.

## dox_cache

### 3.0.0-alpha.8

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.7

- Perf: the memory driver removes expired items and expired locks in a sweep after many writes. Before, a key that was written once with a ttl and never read again stayed in memory forever.
- Perf: the memory driver with no `max_size` does not reorder the map on every hit. The order is only needed for LRU.
- Perf: a tagged cache reads all tag versions with one `many` call (one `MGET` on Redis). `tags(...).flush()` raises all tag versions at the same time. Before, each tag was one round trip after the other.
- Perf: the Redis driver frees a lock with `EVALSHA`. It sends the full script only when Redis does not know it yet.
- Perf: the file driver makes the cache folder only when it is missing. Before, it ran `create(recursive: true)` on every write. Lock tokens use one shared `Random.secure()`.

### 3.0.0-alpha.6

- New `CacheManager.close()`. It closes the connections of every store that was built. The Redis driver closes its connection and its pool connections, with no reconnect. Memory, file and null stores do nothing. It is safe to call twice. A store used after it is built again.
- New `CacheDriver.close()`, for one driver. Custom drivers can override it. The default does nothing.

### 3.0.0-alpha.5

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- New: `getRaw(key)` gives the stored value as JSON text, with no decode. Use it to send a cached value as a JSON response. Memory and Redis return the stored text as is. A stored String comes back with its quotes (`"bar"`). The stored format did not change, so old values still read the same.
- Faster `get`: a plain store builds the key with no async step. `itemKey` now returns `FutureOr<String>`. Memory `get` costs about 0.6 µs instead of 0.86 µs. Memory `getRaw` costs about 0.3 µs.
- New Redis option `pool_size`: the most connections one store opens (ioredis `maxConnection`). Default is 10, the same as before.
- Uses `ioredis` 2.0.0-alpha.2. It sends all commands on one shared connection and writes them together (auto-pipelining). A Redis read costs much less CPU. The cache now uses one connection per store, so `pool_size` rarely matters.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.

### 3.0.0-alpha.1

- Uses `ioredis` 2. Redis error replies throw `RedisError`.
- Redis: no value size limit by default (was 60 KB). `maxValueBytes` is still there if you want one.
- Redis: `many` uses one `MGET`, `putMany` uses one pipeline, `flush` uses `SCAN` + `DEL` (no Lua).
- First release.
- `CacheManager` with named stores and custom drivers.
- Drivers: memory (with LRU), file, Redis, null.
- `remember`, `pull`, `add`, `increment`, `many`, tags and atomic locks.

## dox

### Unreleased

- `dox make:controller` (`create:controller`) writes `@Inject()` above the class, and no global controller instance. The file shows the typed route to use. The command says to run `build_runner`.
- New `dox make:factory <model>`: makes `db/factories/<model>.factory.dart`.
- New `dox make:seeder <name>`: makes `db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart`, writes the seeder list `db/seeders/seeders.dart` and makes `bin/seed.dart` when it is missing.
- New `dox db:seed [--class=<name>]`: runs `bin/seed.dart`. The default seeder is `DatabaseSeeder`.
- New `dox migration:fresh` (or `migrate:fresh`): drops all tables, then runs all migrations.
- `--seed` after `migration:run`, `migration:refresh` or `migration:fresh` runs the seeders when the migrations end well.

### 3.0.0-alpha.8

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.7

- Breaking: `create:controller` no longer takes `-ws`. Dox uses Socket.IO for realtime now. See the Socket.IO docs for a namespace class.
- Security: `dox create` now copies `.env.example` to `.env` and writes a new random `APP_KEY`. Before, every new app used the same public key from the template. You no longer run `cp .env.example .env`.
- The `.env.example` of the CLI has an empty `APP_KEY`. Run `dox key:generate` to set one.

### 3.0.0-alpha.6

- Fix: `dox key:generate` dropped `.env` lines with more than one `=` (like `DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?sslmode=require`). It also dropped comment lines. Now it only changes the `APP_KEY` line. Every other line stays as it is.
- Fix: `dox create` crashed with `Failed to decode data using encoding 'utf-8'` when the template had a binary file (for example `db/dox.sqlite-shm`). It now skips files that are not UTF-8 text. It only writes a file when its content changes.

### 3.0.0-alpha.5

- Fix: `dox create my_app` without `--version` crashed with a `RangeError`.
- Fix: `dox create` picked the GitHub "latest" template release, which skips pre-releases. During the 3.x alpha that gave the old 2.x template. It now takes the newest template with the same major version as the CLI.
- Fix: `dox env:generate` read `KEY=3000 # note` as text, not as an `int`. A `#` after a space is now a comment.
- Fix: `dox update` ran a plain `dart pub global activate dox`, which skips pre-releases. During the 3.x alpha it installed the old 2.x CLI. It now installs the newest version with the same major version as the CLI, from the pub.dev version list.

### 3.0.0-alpha.4

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.3

- Version bump only, to match the other packages.

### 3.0.0-alpha.2

- Fix: `dox build` no longer passes `--delete-conflicting-outputs` to build_runner (it was removed and printed a warning).
- Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
- All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
- `dox build` now runs `dart build cli` (AOT, with build hooks). The output is `build/bundle/`. Start it with `cd build/bundle && ./bin/server`.
- New `dox create:dto <name>`: makes `lib/app/http/dtos/<name>.dto.dart`. `dox create:request` is removed.
- `dox create:controller -r` uses `int id` for the resource methods.
- New `dox openapi:generate [dir]`. It runs the app's `bin/openapi.dart` and writes `openapi.json` and `openapi.yaml` (default `storage/openapi`).
- New `dox env:generate`: makes `lib/config/env.dart` (the typed env class) from `.env.example`.
- New `dox env:check`: loads the typed env and prints every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

- Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
- Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
